nodes.name: (P2) log-sum via summable K_j-H_j error
nodes.statement: {\flushleft \bf Verification of (P2). } The following lemma is the key to verifying (P2) and (P3), as it establishes a summable error bound between the kernels $\mathcal{K}_j$ and $\mathcal{H}_j$, ensuring the properties of their sum are preserved. \begin{lemma} Let $\mathcal{H}_j$ and $\mathcal{K}_j$ be the positive definite functions defined in \eqref{eq:def-Hj} and \eqref{eq:def-Kj}. Then we have \[ \sum_{j=1}^\infty \|\mathcal{K}_j-\mathcal{H}_j\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^d)}<\infty. \] \end{lemma} \begin{lemma} Let $\mathcal{H}_j$ be the kernel function in \eqref{eq:def-Hj}. Then \[ |\mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{w})|\le C 2^jd_{\mathbb{T}^d}(\boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{w}),\quad \forall \boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{w}\in \mathbb{T}^d, \] where $C$ is a constant independent of $j$. \end{lemma} \begin{proof} Let $\xi_j$ be the Gaussian process in Corollary~\ref{corollary:original-process} and $\boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{w}\in \mathbb{T}^d$. Then, \[ |\mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{w})|=|\mathbb{E}[\xi_j(\boldsymbol{z})\xi_j(\boldsymbol{1})]-\mathbb{E}[\xi_j(\boldsymbol{w})\xi_j(\boldsymbol{1})]|= |\mathbb{E}[\xi_j(\boldsymbol{1})(\xi_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\xi_j(\boldsymbol{w}))]|. \] By Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have \[ |\mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{w})|\le (\mathbb{E}[|\xi_j(\boldsymbol{1})|^2])^{1/2}\cdot (\mathbb{E}[|\xi_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\xi_j(\boldsymbol{w})|^2])^{1/2}. \] Following the same line in the proof of Proposition~\ref{corollary:original-process}, we have \[ \mathbb{E}[|\xi_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\xi_j(\boldsymbol{w})|^2]\le 3C_\Phi 2^{2j}\cdot (d_{\mathbb{T}^d}(\boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{w}))^2. \] Therefore, \[ |\mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{w})|\le (\log 2)^{1/2}\cdot (3C_\Phi )^{1/2}\cdot 2^j d_{\mathbb{T}^d}(\boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{w}). \] This proves the lemma. \end{proof} \begin{proof}[Proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:convergence-difference}] Fix $\boldsymbol{z}=(e(t_1),e(t_2),\ldots,e(t_d))\in \mathbb{T}^d$. By definition, \begin{align*} \mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{z})=(\mathcal{H}_j*P_j*\widetilde{P_j})(\boldsymbol{z})=\iint_{\mathbb{T}^d\times \mathbb{T}^d} P(\boldsymbol{w}_1)P_j(\bar{\boldsymbol{w}}_2)\mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{z}\cdot\overline{\boldsymbol{w}_1\boldsymbol{w}_2})\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{w}_1)\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{w}_2). \end{align*} Since $\operatorname{supp} P_j\subset \mathcal{B}_j$, \begin{align*} \big|\mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{z})\big|&=\bigg|\iint_{\mathbb{T}^d\times \mathbb{T}^d} P(\boldsymbol{w}_1)P_j(\bar{\boldsymbol{w}}_2)(\mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{z}\cdot\overline{\boldsymbol{w}_1\boldsymbol{w}_2})-\mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{z}))\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{w}_1)\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{w}_2)\bigg|\\ &\le \iint_{\mathcal{B}_j\times \mathcal{B}_j}P_j(\boldsymbol{w}_1)P_j(\bar{\boldsymbol{w}}_2)|\mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{z}\cdot\overline{\boldsymbol{w}_1\boldsymbol{w}_2})-\mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{z})|\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{w}_1)\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{w}_2). \end{align*} By Lemma~\ref{lemma:Lipschitz-continuity-kernel}, we have \begin{align*} |\mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{z}\cdot \overline{\boldsymbol{w}_1\boldsymbol{w}_2})-\mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{z})|&\le C2^j d_{\mathbb{T}^d}(\boldsymbol{z}\cdot \overline{\boldsymbol{w}_1\boldsymbol{w}_2},\boldsymbol{z})\\ &=C2^jd_{\mathbb{T}^d}(\boldsymbol{w}_1\boldsymbol{w}_2,\boldsymbol{1}) \\ & \le C2^j\cdot (2j^{-2}2^{-j})=2Cj^{-2}. \end{align*} Therefore, \begin{align*} |\mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{z})|&\le 2Cj^{-2}\cdot \iint_{\mathcal{B}_j\times \mathcal{B}_j} P_j(\boldsymbol{w}_1)P_j(\bar{\boldsymbol{w}}_2)\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{w}_1)\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{w}_2)\\ &=2Cj^{-2}\cdot \iint_{[-1/2,1/2)^d\times [-1/2,1/2)^d} Q_j(\boldsymbol{x})Q_j(-\boldsymbol{y})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{x}\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{y}\\ &=2Cj^{-2}\cdot \bigg(\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} Q_j(\boldsymbol{x})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{x}\bigg)^2=2Cj^{-2}. \end{align*} Since the choice of $\boldsymbol{z}$ is arbitrary, we have \[ \sum_{j=1}^\infty \|\mathcal{K}_j-\mathcal{H}_j\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^d)}\le 2C\cdot \sum_{j=1}^\infty j^{-2}<\infty. \] This completes the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:convergence-difference}. \end{proof} Define \[ g_1(\boldsymbol{z})\coloneq \sum_{j=1}^\infty (\mathcal{K}_j-\mathcal{H}_j)(\boldsymbol{z}),\quad \forall \boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d. \] Then, by Lemma~\ref{lemma:convergence-difference}, the function $g_1$ is continuous on $\mathbb{T}^d$. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:properties-Hj}, we have \[ \sum_{j=1}^\infty \mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{z})=\log \frac{1}{\|\boldsymbol{z}\|_{\mathbb{T}^d}}+g_0(\|\boldsymbol{z}\|_{\mathbb{T}^d}),\quad \forall \boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d\setminus\{\boldsymbol{1}\}, \] where $g_0\in C^1([0,\sqrt{d}])$. Let $g(\boldsymbol{z})\coloneq g_1(\boldsymbol{z})+g_0(\|\boldsymbol{z}\|_{\mathbb{T}^d})$, then $g$ is continuous on $\mathbb{T}^d$. Thus, for all $\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d\setminus\{\boldsymbol{1}\}$, we have \begin{align*} \sum_{j=1}^\infty \mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{z})&=\sum_{j=1}^\infty (\mathcal{K}_j-\mathcal{H}_j)(\boldsymbol{z})+\sum_{j=1}^\infty \mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{z})\\ &=g_1(\boldsymbol{z})+\log_+ \frac{1}{\|\boldsymbol{z}\|_{\mathbb{T}^d}}+g_0(\|\boldsymbol{z}\|_{\mathbb{T}^d})\\ &=\log_+ \frac{1}{\|\boldsymbol{z}\|_{\mathbb{T}^d}}+g(\boldsymbol{z}). \end{align*} This completes the verification of (P2).

nodes.name: (P3) limiting variance log 2
nodes.statement: {\flushleft \bf Verification of (P3). } By definition of $\mathcal{H}_j$ and \eqref{eq:properties-Phi}, we have \[ \mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{1})=\mathcal{L}_j(\boldsymbol{0})=\int_1^2 \frac{\Phi(\boldsymbol{0})}{u}\,\mathrm{d}u=\log 2. \]

nodes.name: (P4) derivative bounds via derivatives of P_j
nodes.statement: {\flushleft \bf Verification of (P4). } Inspired by \eqref{eq:diff-convolution} in Lemma~\ref{lemma:convolution-deterministic}, it is necessary to control the $L^\infty$-norm of derivatives of $P_j$. \begin{lemma} For any multi-index $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$ with $|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|\le d$ and $j\ge 1$, we have \[ \|D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} P_j(\boldsymbol{z})\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^d)}\le j^{2(|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|+d)}2^{j(|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|+d)}\|Q\|_{C^d(\mathbb{R}^d)}. \] \end{lemma} \begin{proof} By the definition of $P_j$, we have \[ D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} P_j(\boldsymbol{z})=j^{2d}2^{jd}D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} Q_j(\boldsymbol{t}), \] where $\boldsymbol{t}=(t_1,t_2,\ldots,t_d)$ is the canonical representation of $\boldsymbol{z}$ in $[-1/2,1/2)^d$ and $\varepsilon_j=j^{-2}2^{-j}$. By the chain rule, we have \[ \bigg(\partial^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} Q\bigg(\frac{\cdot}{\varepsilon_j}\bigg)\bigg)(\boldsymbol{t})=\varepsilon_j^{-|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|}(\partial^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} Q)\bigg(\frac{\boldsymbol{t}}{\varepsilon_j}\bigg)=j^{2|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|}2^{j|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|}(\partial^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} Q)\bigg(\frac{\boldsymbol{t}}{\varepsilon_j}\bigg). \] Therefore, \[ \|D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} P_j(\boldsymbol{z})\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^d)}=j^{2(|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|+d)}2^{j(\boldsymbol{\alpha}|+d)}\|\partial^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} Q\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)}\le j^{2(|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|+d)}2^{j(|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|+d)}\cdot\|Q\|_{C^d(\mathbb{R}^d)}. \] This proves the lemma. \end{proof} By Lemma~\ref{lemma:mollification-Gaussian-process}, we know \[ (D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} \psi_j)(\boldsymbol{z})=D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} (P_j*\xi_j)(\boldsymbol{z})=((D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} P_j)*\xi_j)(\boldsymbol{z}). \] Recalling that $\operatorname{supp} P_j\subset \mathcal{B}_j$ in \eqref{eq:supp-Pj}, we have \begin{align*} |D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} \psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})|&\le \int_{\mathcal{B}_j}\|D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} P_j\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^d)}\cdot |\xi_j(\boldsymbol{z})|\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z})\\ &\le \|Q\|_{C^d(\mathbb{R}^d)}\cdot j^{2(|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|+d)}2^{j(|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|+d)}\cdot \int_{\mathcal{B}_j}|\xi_j(\boldsymbol{z})|\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z}). \end{align*} Let $0<p<\infty$. The $p$-moment of $D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\psi_j$ can be estimated by \[ \mathbb{E}[|D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} \psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]\le \|Q\|_{C^d(\mathbb{R}^d)}^p\cdot j^{2(|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|+d)p}2^{j(|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|+d)p}\cdot \mathbb{E}\bigg[\bigg|\int_{\mathcal{B}_j}|\xi_j(\boldsymbol{z})|\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z})\bigg|^p\bigg]. \] By Minkowski's inequality and Lemma~\ref{lemma:Lp-Gaussian-equiv}, we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\bigg[\bigg|\int_{\mathcal{B}_j}|\xi_j(\boldsymbol{z})|\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z})\bigg|^p\bigg]&\le \bigg\{\int_{\mathcal{B}_j}\big(\mathbb{E}[|\xi_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]\big)^{1/p}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z})\bigg\}^p\\ &=2^{p/2}\bigg(\frac{\Gamma((p+1)/2)}{\sqrt{\pi}}\bigg)\cdot \bigg\{\int_{\mathcal{B}_j}\big(\mathbb{E}[|\xi_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^2]\big)^{1/2}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z})\bigg\}^p\\ &=2^{p/2}\bigg(\frac{\Gamma((p+1)/2)}{\sqrt{\pi}}\bigg)\cdot \bigg\{\int_{\mathcal{B}_j}\big(\mathcal{H}_j(\boldsymbol{1})\big)^{1/2}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z})\bigg\}^p\\ &=(2\log 2)^{p/2}\bigg(\frac{\Gamma((p+1)/2)}{\sqrt{\pi}}\bigg)\cdot (\Omega_d j^{-2d}2^{-jd})^p, \end{align*} where $\Omega_d$ is the volume of unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Denote \[ \Theta(p)=\max\bigg\{1,\|Q\|_{C^d(\mathbb{R}^d)}^p\cdot (2\log 2)^{p/2}\cdot \bigg(\frac{\Gamma((p+1)/2)}{\sqrt{\pi}}\bigg)\cdot \Omega_d^p\bigg\}. \] Then for all $0<p<\infty$, we have \[ \sup_{j}\sup_{|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|\le d}\sup_{z\in \mathbb{T}^d}\frac{\mathbb{E}\big[|D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} \psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p\big]}{j^{2|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|p}2^{j|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|p}}\le \Theta(p). \] We claim that $\Theta$ is increasing in $p$. Let $f(p)=\big(\frac{\Gamma((p+1)/2)}{\sqrt{\pi}}\big)^{1/p}$. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:Lp-Gaussian-equiv} and Lyapunov's inequality, we can see that $f(p)$ is increasing in $p$. It follows that \[ \Theta(p)=\max\Big\{1,\big(\|Q\|_{C^d(\mathbb{R}^d)}\cdot (2\log2)^{1/2}\cdot \Omega_d\cdot f(p)\big)^p\Big\} \] is increasing in $p$ as well. Hence the constructed processes satisfy (P4).

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1.2
nodes.statement: The natural filtration $(\mathscr{G}_{m})_{m\ge 1}$ is defined by \[ \mathscr{G}_m\coloneq \sigma\{X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_m\}, \] that is, the $\sigma$-algebra generated by the random processes $X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_m$ introduced in \eqref{eq:def-Xj}. \medskip {\flushleft \bf Step 1. Decoupling of different scales.} \medskip \begin{lemma} The sequence of random vectors $\{(\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\widehat{\mu}_m(\boldsymbol{n}))_{\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d}:m\ge 1\}$ is an $\ell^q$-vector-valued martingale. \end{lemma} \begin{proof} The integrability condition $\mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{M}_m\|_{l^q}] < \infty$ holds for any finite $m$ due to the $C^\infty$-smoothness of the sample paths of $\mu_m$ (a consequence of (P0) in Proposition~\ref{prop:smooth-decomposition-log-correlated-field}). For each $m\ge 2$ and $\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d$, we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}[\widehat{\mu}_m(\boldsymbol{n})-\widehat{\mu}_{m-1}(\boldsymbol{n})|\mathscr{G}_{m-1}]=\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\mathbb{E}\Big[\big[\prod_{j=1}^m X_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\prod_{j=1}^{m-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\big]\Big| \mathscr{G}_{m-1}\Big]\boldsymbol{z}^{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z}). \end{align*} Since $X_m$ is independent of $\mathscr{G}_{m-1}$ and $X_j$ is $\mathscr{G}_{m-1}$-measurable for each $1\le j\le m-1$, we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\Big[\big[\prod_{j=1}^m X_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\prod_{j=1}^{m-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\big]\Big| \mathscr{G}_{m-1}\Big]&=\big(\mathbb{E}[X_m|\mathscr{G}_{m-1}]-1\big)\cdot \prod_{j=1}^{m-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\\ &=\big(\mathbb{E}[X_m]-1\big)\cdot \prod_{j=1}^{m-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})=0. \end{align*} Therefore, we have \[ \mathbb{E}[\widehat{\mu}_m(\boldsymbol{n})-\widehat{\mu}_{m-1}(\boldsymbol{n})|\mathscr{G}_{m-1}]=0, \] which implies that $\{(\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\widehat{\mu}_m(\boldsymbol{n}))_{\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d}:m\ge 1\}$ is an $\ell^q$-vector-valued martingale with respect to the filtration $\{\mathscr{G}_m\}_{m\ge 1}$. \end{proof} Denote the $\ell^q$-vector-valued martingale $\{(\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\widehat{\mu}_m(\boldsymbol{n}))_{\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d}:m\ge 1\}$ by $(\mathcal{M}_m)_{m\ge 1}$. Then we apply \eqref{eq:def-Mtype} on $\mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{M}_m\|_{\ell^q}^p]$ to decouple components with different scales of $\mu_m$ by \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{M}_m\|_{\ell^q}^p]\lesssim \sum_{k=1}^m \mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{M}_{k}-\mathcal{M}_{k-1}\|_{\ell^q}^p]. \end{equation} \medskip {\flushleft \bf Step 2. Decoupling the spatially localized components.} \medskip For each $k\ge 1$ and $\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k$, define \[ \mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n})\coloneq \langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}(\boldsymbol{z})\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\boldsymbol{z})\cdot \boldsymbol{z}^{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z}), \] where $\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d\setminus\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$ and \[ \mathring{X}_k(\boldsymbol{z})=X_k(\boldsymbol{z})-\mathbb{E}[X_k(\boldsymbol{z})]=X_k(\boldsymbol{z})-1. \] Recall that \[ \mathcal{M}_k-\mathcal{M}_{k-1}=\bigg(\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\boldsymbol{z})\boldsymbol{z}^{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z})\bigg)_{\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d}. \] We insert the partition of unity $\{\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}\}_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k}$ into the integral above to obtain \begin{align*} \langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\boldsymbol{z})\boldsymbol{z}^{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z})&=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\boldsymbol{z})\Big(\sum_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k}\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}(\boldsymbol{z})\Big)\boldsymbol{z}^{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z})\\ &=\sum_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k}\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\boldsymbol{z})\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}(\boldsymbol{z})\boldsymbol{z}^{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z})\\ &=\sum_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k}\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n}). \end{align*} It turns out that we can divide $\sum_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k}\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n})$ into finite parts. The summands in each part are conditionally independent, which allows us to apply \eqref{eq:def-ind-Mtype} to obtain the estimate of $\mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{M}_k-\mathcal{M}_{k-1}\|_{\ell^q}^p]$. Now we make the assertion above clear. Define an equivalence relation on $\mathscr{D}_k$ by \[ \boldsymbol{I}\sim \boldsymbol{I}'\quad \text{if and only if}\quad \boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}}-\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}'}\in (5\cdot 2^{-k})\mathbb{Z}^d. \] Thereby, we can partition $\mathscr{D}_k$ into disjoint subfamilies $\{\mathscr{D}_{k,s}\}_{s=1}^{S_k}$. These unordered subfamilies can be uniquely determined by the following two features. \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] For any $\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_{k,s}$, we have \[ \mathscr{D}_{k,s}=\{\boldsymbol{I}'\in \mathscr{D}_k:\boldsymbol{I}'\sim \boldsymbol{I}\}. \] \item[(2)] The family of $k$-th generation dyadic cubes $\mathscr{D}_k$ can be decomposed as \[ \mathscr{D}_k=\bigsqcup_{s=1}^{S_k}\mathscr{D}_{k,s}. \] \end{itemize} \begin{lemma} Let $\mathscr{D}_{k,s}$ be the $s$-th subfamily of $\mathscr{D}_k$ defined above. Then the following properties hold: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] For any $s\in \{1,2,\ldots,S_k\}$ and different $\boldsymbol{I},\boldsymbol{I}'\in \mathscr{D}_{k,s}$, $\{X_k(\boldsymbol{z})\}_{\boldsymbol{z}\in 2\boldsymbol{I}}$ and $\{X_k(\boldsymbol{z})\}_{\boldsymbol{z}\in 2\boldsymbol{I}'}$ are independent. \item[(2)] The number of partitions $S_k$ can be bounded by a constant $S(d)\coloneq 5^d$. \end{itemize} \end{lemma} \begin{proof} (1). Let $\boldsymbol{I},\boldsymbol{I}'\in \mathscr{D}_{k,s}$ and $\boldsymbol{I}\ne \boldsymbol{I}'$. Then for any $\boldsymbol{z}\in 2\boldsymbol{I}$, $\boldsymbol{z}'\in 2\boldsymbol{I}'$, we have $d_{\mathbb{T}^d}(\boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{z}')\ge 3\cdot 2^{-k}$. By (P1) in Proposition~\ref{prop:smooth-decomposition-log-correlated-field}, we know that if $d_{\mathbb{T}^d}(\boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{z}')\ge 3\cdot 2^{-k}$, then \[ \mathbb{E}[X_k(\boldsymbol{z})X_k(\boldsymbol{z}')]=K_k(\boldsymbol{z}\cdot \overline{\boldsymbol{z}'})=0, \] that is, $X_k(\boldsymbol{z})$ and $X_k(\boldsymbol{z}')$ are independent. This proves (1). (2). Fix a cube $\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_{k,1}$, whose center $\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}}=(c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_d)$. Then for any $\mathscr{D}_{k,s}$, we can pick a unique cube $\boldsymbol{I}_s\in \mathscr{D}_{k,s}$, such that the center of $\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}_s}=(c_{s,1},c_{s,2},\ldots,c_{s,d})$ satisfying $c_{s,j}-c_{j}\in \{b\cdot 2^{-k}:b=0,1,\ldots,4\}$. In other words, the center of $\boldsymbol{I}_s$ can be written as \[ \boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}_s}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}}+2^{-k}\boldsymbol{b}_s, \] for some $\boldsymbol{b}_s=(b_{s,1},b_{s,2},\ldots,b_{s,d})\in \{0,1,2,3,4\}^d$. This gives an injection from $\{\mathscr{D}_{k,s}:s=1,2,\ldots,R_k\}$ to $\{0,1,2,3,4\}^d$, which provides us the upper bound of the number of partitions $S_k\le 5^d$. \end{proof} We can now estimate $\mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{M}_k-\mathcal{M}_{k-1}\|_{\ell^q}^p]$ by \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{M}_k-\mathcal{M}_{k-1}\|_{\ell^q}^p]\le |S_k|^{p-1} \sum_{s=1}^{S_k}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\bigg\|\sum_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_{k,s}}\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\bigg\|_{\ell^q}^p\bigg]\lesssim \sum_{s=1}^{S_k}\sum_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_{k,s}}\mathbb{E}[\|\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\|_{\ell^q}^p]=\sum_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k}\mathbb{E}[\|\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\|_{\ell^q}^p], \end{align*} where the second inequality follows from \eqref{eq:def-ind-Mtype-scalar} and the implicit constant is independent of $k$. \medskip {\flushleft \bf Step 3. Applying the local estimate and conclusion.} \medskip \begin{proposition} For each $k\ge 1$ and $\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k$, we have the estimate \[ \mathbb{E}[\|\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\|_{\ell^q}^p]\lesssim k^{4dp} 2^{k(-dp+dp/q+\tau p/2)}\sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^k \big(\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]\big)\bigg]. \] \end{proposition} \begin{lemma} For any $0<p<\infty$, we have \[ \lim_{j\to \infty}\sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]=2^{p(p-1)\gamma^2/2}. \] \end{lemma} \begin{proof} Fix $\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d$. We have \[ \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]=\mathbb{E}\big[\exp\big(p\gamma \psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\frac{p\gamma^2}{2}\mathbb{E}[\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})^2]\big)\big]=\exp\bigg(\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}\mathbb{E}[\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})^2]\bigg). \] Recalling that the kernel function of $\psi_j$ is $\mathcal{K}_j$, hence \[ \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]=\exp\bigg(\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}\mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{1})\bigg), \] which is independent of $\boldsymbol{z}$. Combining (P2) in Proposition~\ref{prop:smooth-decomposition-log-correlated-field}, we have \[ \lim_{j\to \infty}\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]=\lim_{j\to \infty}\exp\bigg(\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}\mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{1})\bigg)=\exp\bigg(\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}\log 2\bigg)=2^{p(p-1)\gamma^2/2}. \] This proves the desired limit. \end{proof} Lemma~\ref{lemma:p-moment-Xj} implies that for any $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a constant $M_{\varepsilon}>0$, such that \[ \sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^k\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]\bigg]\le M_{\varepsilon}2^{kp(p-1)\gamma^2/2+\varepsilon},\quad \forall k\ge 1. \] By Proposition~\ref{prop:localization}, we have \begin{align*} \sum_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k}\mathbb{E}[\|\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\|_{\ell^q}^p]&\lesssim 2^{kd}\cdot k^{4dp} 2^{k(-dp+dp/q+\tau p/2)}\sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^k \big(\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]\big)\bigg]\\ &\lesssim k^{4dp} 2^{k(-(p-1)d+dp/q+\tau p/2)}\cdot 2^{kp(p-1)\gamma^2/2+\varepsilon}. \end{align*} Combining this with \eqref{eq:decoupling-martingale}, we obtain \begin{align} \notag \mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{M}_m\|_{\ell^q}^p]&\lesssim \sum_{k=1}^m k^{4dp} 2^{k(-(p-1)d+dp/q+\tau p/2)}\cdot 2^{kp(p-1)\gamma^2/2+\varepsilon}\\ &\lesssim \sum_{k=1}^\infty k^{4dp} 2^{k(-(p-1)d+dp/q+\tau p/2)}\cdot 2^{kp(p-1)\gamma^2/2+\varepsilon}. \end{align} The series above converges if and only if $-(p-1)d+dp/q+\tau p/2+p(p-1)\gamma^2/2+\varepsilon<0$. Define \[ \zeta(p)=2d+\gamma^2-\bigg(\frac{2d}{p}+p\gamma^2\bigg). \] Thus, for any $\tau>0$ satisfying \[ \tau<\sup_{1\le p\le 2}\zeta(p), \] we can choose $q$ and $\varepsilon$, such that the series \eqref{eq:series-moment-estimate-Mm} converges. An elementary computation shows that \begin{itemize} \item If $0<\gamma<\sqrt{2d}/2$, then $\sup_{1\le p\le 2}\zeta(p)=\zeta(2)=d-\gamma^2$. \item If $\sqrt{2d}/2\le \gamma<\sqrt{2d}$, then $\sup_{1\le p\le 2}\zeta(p)=\zeta(\sqrt{2d}/\gamma)=(\sqrt{2d}-\gamma)^2$. \end{itemize} This proves Proposition~\ref{prop:uniform-boundedness-Fourier-Lebesgue-norm}.
nodes.statement_short: Vector-valued martingale method: Pisier's type-p inequality decouples scales, finite dependence decouples locations, then sum the local estimate of Prop 4.4. The key step is choosing p in [1,2] maximizing zeta(p).

nodes.name: Step 3: apply local estimate and sum the series
nodes.statement: {\flushleft \bf Step 3. Applying the local estimate and conclusion.} \medskip \begin{proposition} For each $k\ge 1$ and $\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k$, we have the estimate \[ \mathbb{E}[\|\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\|_{\ell^q}^p]\lesssim k^{4dp} 2^{k(-dp+dp/q+\tau p/2)}\sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^k \big(\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]\big)\bigg]. \] \end{proposition} \begin{lemma} For any $0<p<\infty$, we have \[ \lim_{j\to \infty}\sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]=2^{p(p-1)\gamma^2/2}. \] \end{lemma} \begin{proof} Fix $\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d$. We have \[ \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]=\mathbb{E}\big[\exp\big(p\gamma \psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\frac{p\gamma^2}{2}\mathbb{E}[\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})^2]\big)\big]=\exp\bigg(\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}\mathbb{E}[\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})^2]\bigg). \] Recalling that the kernel function of $\psi_j$ is $\mathcal{K}_j$, hence \[ \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]=\exp\bigg(\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}\mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{1})\bigg), \] which is independent of $\boldsymbol{z}$. Combining (P2) in Proposition~\ref{prop:smooth-decomposition-log-correlated-field}, we have \[ \lim_{j\to \infty}\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]=\lim_{j\to \infty}\exp\bigg(\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}\mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{1})\bigg)=\exp\bigg(\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}\log 2\bigg)=2^{p(p-1)\gamma^2/2}. \] This proves the desired limit. \end{proof} Lemma~\ref{lemma:p-moment-Xj} implies that for any $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a constant $M_{\varepsilon}>0$, such that \[ \sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^k\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]\bigg]\le M_{\varepsilon}2^{kp(p-1)\gamma^2/2+\varepsilon},\quad \forall k\ge 1. \] By Proposition~\ref{prop:localization}, we have \begin{align*} \sum_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k}\mathbb{E}[\|\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\|_{\ell^q}^p]&\lesssim 2^{kd}\cdot k^{4dp} 2^{k(-dp+dp/q+\tau p/2)}\sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^k \big(\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]\big)\bigg]\\ &\lesssim k^{4dp} 2^{k(-(p-1)d+dp/q+\tau p/2)}\cdot 2^{kp(p-1)\gamma^2/2+\varepsilon}. \end{align*} Combining this with \eqref{eq:decoupling-martingale}, we obtain \begin{align} \notag \mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{M}_m\|_{\ell^q}^p]&\lesssim \sum_{k=1}^m k^{4dp} 2^{k(-(p-1)d+dp/q+\tau p/2)}\cdot 2^{kp(p-1)\gamma^2/2+\varepsilon}\\ &\lesssim \sum_{k=1}^\infty k^{4dp} 2^{k(-(p-1)d+dp/q+\tau p/2)}\cdot 2^{kp(p-1)\gamma^2/2+\varepsilon}. \end{align} The series above converges if and only if $-(p-1)d+dp/q+\tau p/2+p(p-1)\gamma^2/2+\varepsilon<0$. Define \[ \zeta(p)=2d+\gamma^2-\bigg(\frac{2d}{p}+p\gamma^2\bigg). \] Thus, for any $\tau>0$ satisfying \[ \tau<\sup_{1\le p\le 2}\zeta(p), \] we can choose $q$ and $\varepsilon$, such that the series \eqref{eq:series-moment-estimate-Mm} converges. An elementary computation shows that \begin{itemize} \item If $0<\gamma<\sqrt{2d}/2$, then $\sup_{1\le p\le 2}\zeta(p)=\zeta(2)=d-\gamma^2$. \item If $\sqrt{2d}/2\le \gamma<\sqrt{2d}$, then $\sup_{1\le p\le 2}\zeta(p)=\zeta(\sqrt{2d}/\gamma)=(\sqrt{2d}-\gamma)^2$. \end{itemize} This proves Proposition~\ref{prop:uniform-boundedness-Fourier-Lebesgue-norm}.
nodes.statement_short: Step 3: apply local estimate and sum the series

nodes.name: Define localized coefficients D_I^phi
nodes.statement: For each $k\ge 1$ and $\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k$, define \[ \mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n})\coloneq \langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}(\boldsymbol{z})\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\boldsymbol{z})\cdot \boldsymbol{z}^{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z}), \] where $\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d\setminus\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$ and \[ \mathring{X}_k(\boldsymbol{z})=X_k(\boldsymbol{z})-\mathbb{E}[X_k(\boldsymbol{z})]=X_k(\boldsymbol{z})-1. \]

nodes.name: Insert the partition of unity
nodes.statement: Recall that \[ \mathcal{M}_k-\mathcal{M}_{k-1}=\bigg(\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\boldsymbol{z})\boldsymbol{z}^{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z})\bigg)_{\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d}. \] We insert the partition of unity $\{\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}\}_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k}$ into the integral above to obtain \begin{align*} \langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\boldsymbol{z})\boldsymbol{z}^{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z})&=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\boldsymbol{z})\Big(\sum_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k}\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}(\boldsymbol{z})\Big)\boldsymbol{z}^{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z})\\ &=\sum_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k}\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\boldsymbol{z})\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}(\boldsymbol{z})\boldsymbol{z}^{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z})\\ &=\sum_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k}\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n}). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Insert the partition of unity: M_k-M_{k-1} = sum of D_I^phi

nodes.name: Group cubes into classes spaced 5*2^{-k} apart
nodes.statement: It turns out that we can divide $\sum_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k}\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n})$ into finite parts. The summands in each part are conditionally independent, which allows us to apply \eqref{eq:def-ind-Mtype} to obtain the estimate of $\mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{M}_k-\mathcal{M}_{k-1}\|_{\ell^q}^p]$. Now we make the assertion above clear. Define an equivalence relation on $\mathscr{D}_k$ by \[ \boldsymbol{I}\sim \boldsymbol{I}'\quad \text{if and only if}\quad \boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}}-\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}'}\in (5\cdot 2^{-k})\mathbb{Z}^d. \] Thereby, we can partition $\mathscr{D}_k$ into disjoint subfamilies $\{\mathscr{D}_{k,s}\}_{s=1}^{S_k}$. These unordered subfamilies can be uniquely determined by the following two features.
nodes.statement_short: Group cubes into classes spaced 5*2^{-k} apart

nodes.name: (1) Each class is an equivalence class
nodes.statement: [(1)] For any $\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_{k,s}$, we have \[ \mathscr{D}_{k,s}=\{\boldsymbol{I}'\in \mathscr{D}_k:\boldsymbol{I}'\sim \boldsymbol{I}\}. \]
nodes.statement_short: (1) Each class is an equivalence class

nodes.name: (2) Classes partition D_k
nodes.statement: [(2)] The family of $k$-th generation dyadic cubes $\mathscr{D}_k$ can be decomposed as \[ \mathscr{D}_k=\bigsqcup_{s=1}^{S_k}\mathscr{D}_{k,s}. \]

nodes.name: Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement: \begin{lemma} Let $\mathscr{D}_{k,s}$ be the $s$-th subfamily of $\mathscr{D}_k$ defined above. Then the following properties hold: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] For any $s\in \{1,2,\ldots,S_k\}$ and different $\boldsymbol{I},\boldsymbol{I}'\in \mathscr{D}_{k,s}$, $\{X_k(\boldsymbol{z})\}_{\boldsymbol{z}\in 2\boldsymbol{I}}$ and $\{X_k(\boldsymbol{z})\}_{\boldsymbol{z}\in 2\boldsymbol{I}'}$ are independent. \item[(2)] The number of partitions $S_k$ can be bounded by a constant $S(d)\coloneq 5^d$. \end{itemize} \end{lemma} \begin{proof} (1). Let $\boldsymbol{I},\boldsymbol{I}'\in \mathscr{D}_{k,s}$ and $\boldsymbol{I}\ne \boldsymbol{I}'$. Then for any $\boldsymbol{z}\in 2\boldsymbol{I}$, $\boldsymbol{z}'\in 2\boldsymbol{I}'$, we have $d_{\mathbb{T}^d}(\boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{z}')\ge 3\cdot 2^{-k}$. By (P1) in Proposition~\ref{prop:smooth-decomposition-log-correlated-field}, we know that if $d_{\mathbb{T}^d}(\boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{z}')\ge 3\cdot 2^{-k}$, then \[ \mathbb{E}[X_k(\boldsymbol{z})X_k(\boldsymbol{z}')]=K_k(\boldsymbol{z}\cdot \overline{\boldsymbol{z}'})=0, \] that is, $X_k(\boldsymbol{z})$ and $X_k(\boldsymbol{z}')$ are independent. This proves (1). (2). Fix a cube $\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_{k,1}$, whose center $\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}}=(c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_d)$. Then for any $\mathscr{D}_{k,s}$, we can pick a unique cube $\boldsymbol{I}_s\in \mathscr{D}_{k,s}$, such that the center of $\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}_s}=(c_{s,1},c_{s,2},\ldots,c_{s,d})$ satisfying $c_{s,j}-c_{j}\in \{b\cdot 2^{-k}:b=0,1,\ldots,4\}$. In other words, the center of $\boldsymbol{I}_s$ can be written as \[ \boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}_s}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}}+2^{-k}\boldsymbol{b}_s, \] for some $\boldsymbol{b}_s=(b_{s,1},b_{s,2},\ldots,b_{s,d})\in \{0,1,2,3,4\}^d$. This gives an injection from $\{\mathscr{D}_{k,s}:s=1,2,\ldots,R_k\}$ to $\{0,1,2,3,4\}^d$, which provides us the upper bound of the number of partitions $S_k\le 5^d$. \end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.3: independence within classes, at most 5^d classes

nodes.name: Apply the independent type-p inequality class by class
nodes.statement: We can now estimate $\mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{M}_k-\mathcal{M}_{k-1}\|_{\ell^q}^p]$ by \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{M}_k-\mathcal{M}_{k-1}\|_{\ell^q}^p]\le |S_k|^{p-1} \sum_{s=1}^{S_k}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\bigg\|\sum_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_{k,s}}\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\bigg\|_{\ell^q}^p\bigg]\lesssim \sum_{s=1}^{S_k}\sum_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_{k,s}}\mathbb{E}[\|\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\|_{\ell^q}^p]=\sum_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k}\mathbb{E}[\|\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\|_{\ell^q}^p], \end{align*} where the second inequality follows from \eqref{eq:def-ind-Mtype-scalar} and the implicit constant is independent of $k$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the independent type-p inequality class by class

nodes.name: Weighted Fourier coefficients of mu_m form an l^q-valued martingale
nodes.statement: The sequence of random vectors $\{(\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\widehat{\mu}_m(\boldsymbol{n}))_{\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d}:m\ge 1\}$ is an $\ell^q$-vector-valued martingale.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement: The integrability condition $\mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{M}_m\|_{l^q}] < \infty$ holds for any finite $m$ due to the $C^\infty$-smoothness of the sample paths of $\mu_m$ (a consequence of (P0) in Proposition~\ref{prop:smooth-decomposition-log-correlated-field}). For each $m\ge 2$ and $\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d$, we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}[\widehat{\mu}_m(\boldsymbol{n})-\widehat{\mu}_{m-1}(\boldsymbol{n})|\mathscr{G}_{m-1}]=\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\mathbb{E}\Big[\big[\prod_{j=1}^m X_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\prod_{j=1}^{m-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\big]\Big| \mathscr{G}_{m-1}\Big]\boldsymbol{z}^{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z}). \end{align*} Since $X_m$ is independent of $\mathscr{G}_{m-1}$ and $X_j$ is $\mathscr{G}_{m-1}$-measurable for each $1\le j\le m-1$, we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\Big[\big[\prod_{j=1}^m X_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\prod_{j=1}^{m-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\big]\Big| \mathscr{G}_{m-1}\Big]&=\big(\mathbb{E}[X_m|\mathscr{G}_{m-1}]-1\big)\cdot \prod_{j=1}^{m-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\\ &=\big(\mathbb{E}[X_m]-1\big)\cdot \prod_{j=1}^{m-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})=0. \end{align*} Therefore, we have \[ \mathbb{E}[\widehat{\mu}_m(\boldsymbol{n})-\widehat{\mu}_{m-1}(\boldsymbol{n})|\mathscr{G}_{m-1}]=0, \] which implies that $\{(\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\widehat{\mu}_m(\boldsymbol{n}))_{\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d}:m\ge 1\}$ is an $\ell^q$-vector-valued martingale with respect to the filtration $\{\mathscr{G}_m\}_{m\ge 1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Integrability from smoothness, and the martingale property from independence of X_m and E[X_m]=1.

nodes.name: Integrability from (P0)
nodes.statement: The integrability condition $\mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{M}_m\|_{l^q}] < \infty$ holds for any finite $m$ due to the $C^\infty$-smoothness of the sample paths of $\mu_m$ (a consequence of (P0) in Proposition~\ref{prop:smooth-decomposition-log-correlated-field}).

nodes.name: Write conditional expectation of increment
nodes.statement: For each $m\ge 2$ and $\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d$, we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}[\widehat{\mu}_m(\boldsymbol{n})-\widehat{\mu}_{m-1}(\boldsymbol{n})|\mathscr{G}_{m-1}]=\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\mathbb{E}\Big[\big[\prod_{j=1}^m X_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\prod_{j=1}^{m-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\big]\Big| \mathscr{G}_{m-1}\Big]\boldsymbol{z}^{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z}). \end{align*}

nodes.name: Independence and E[X_m]=1 kill the increment
nodes.statement: Since $X_m$ is independent of $\mathscr{G}_{m-1}$ and $X_j$ is $\mathscr{G}_{m-1}$-measurable for each $1\le j\le m-1$, we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\Big[\big[\prod_{j=1}^m X_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\prod_{j=1}^{m-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\big]\Big| \mathscr{G}_{m-1}\Big]&=\big(\mathbb{E}[X_m|\mathscr{G}_{m-1}]-1\big)\cdot \prod_{j=1}^{m-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\\ &=\big(\mathbb{E}[X_m]-1\big)\cdot \prod_{j=1}^{m-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})=0. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Independence and E[X_m]=1 kill the increment

nodes.name: Martingale property
nodes.statement: Therefore, we have \[ \mathbb{E}[\widehat{\mu}_m(\boldsymbol{n})-\widehat{\mu}_{m-1}(\boldsymbol{n})|\mathscr{G}_{m-1}]=0, \] which implies that $\{(\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\widehat{\mu}_m(\boldsymbol{n}))_{\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d}:m\ge 1\}$ is an $\ell^q$-vector-valued martingale with respect to the filtration $\{\mathscr{G}_m\}_{m\ge 1}$.

nodes.name: Decoupling of scales
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{M}_m\|_{\ell^q}^p]\lesssim \sum_{k=1}^m \mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{M}_{k}-\mathcal{M}_{k-1}\|_{\ell^q}^p].
nodes.label: eq:decoupling-martingale

nodes.name: Independent subfamilies of dyadic cubes
nodes.statement: Let $\mathscr{D}_{k,s}$ be the $s$-th subfamily of $\mathscr{D}_k$ defined above. Then the following properties hold: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] For any $s\in \{1,2,\ldots,S_k\}$ and different $\boldsymbol{I},\boldsymbol{I}'\in \mathscr{D}_{k,s}$, $\{X_k(\boldsymbol{z})\}_{\boldsymbol{z}\in 2\boldsymbol{I}}$ and $\{X_k(\boldsymbol{z})\}_{\boldsymbol{z}\in 2\boldsymbol{I}'}$ are independent. \item[(2)] The number of partitions $S_k$ can be bounded by a constant $S(d)\coloneq 5^d$. \end{itemize}
conclusions: $\{X_k(\boldsymbol{z})\}_{\boldsymbol{z}\in 2\boldsymbol{I}}$ and $\{X_k(\boldsymbol{z})\}_{\boldsymbol{z}\in 2\boldsymbol{I}'}$ are independent.
The number of partitions $S_k$ can be bounded by a constant $S(d)\coloneq 5^d$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement: (1). Let $\boldsymbol{I},\boldsymbol{I}'\in \mathscr{D}_{k,s}$ and $\boldsymbol{I}\ne \boldsymbol{I}'$. Then for any $\boldsymbol{z}\in 2\boldsymbol{I}$, $\boldsymbol{z}'\in 2\boldsymbol{I}'$, we have $d_{\mathbb{T}^d}(\boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{z}')\ge 3\cdot 2^{-k}$. By (P1) in Proposition~\ref{prop:smooth-decomposition-log-correlated-field}, we know that if $d_{\mathbb{T}^d}(\boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{z}')\ge 3\cdot 2^{-k}$, then \[ \mathbb{E}[X_k(\boldsymbol{z})X_k(\boldsymbol{z}')]=K_k(\boldsymbol{z}\cdot \overline{\boldsymbol{z}'})=0, \] that is, $X_k(\boldsymbol{z})$ and $X_k(\boldsymbol{z}')$ are independent. This proves (1). (2). Fix a cube $\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_{k,1}$, whose center $\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}}=(c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_d)$. Then for any $\mathscr{D}_{k,s}$, we can pick a unique cube $\boldsymbol{I}_s\in \mathscr{D}_{k,s}$, such that the center of $\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}_s}=(c_{s,1},c_{s,2},\ldots,c_{s,d})$ satisfying $c_{s,j}-c_{j}\in \{b\cdot 2^{-k}:b=0,1,\ldots,4\}$. In other words, the center of $\boldsymbol{I}_s$ can be written as \[ \boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}_s}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}}+2^{-k}\boldsymbol{b}_s, \] for some $\boldsymbol{b}_s=(b_{s,1},b_{s,2},\ldots,b_{s,d})\in \{0,1,2,3,4\}^d$. This gives an injection from $\{\mathscr{D}_{k,s}:s=1,2,\ldots,R_k\}$ to $\{0,1,2,3,4\}^d$, which provides us the upper bound of the number of partitions $S_k\le 5^d$.
nodes.statement_short: (1) from finite dependence (P1); (2) by injecting the classes into {0,...,4}^d.

nodes.name: (1) Independence via (P1)
nodes.statement: (1). Let $\boldsymbol{I},\boldsymbol{I}'\in \mathscr{D}_{k,s}$ and $\boldsymbol{I}\ne \boldsymbol{I}'$. Then for any $\boldsymbol{z}\in 2\boldsymbol{I}$, $\boldsymbol{z}'\in 2\boldsymbol{I}'$, we have $d_{\mathbb{T}^d}(\boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{z}')\ge 3\cdot 2^{-k}$. By (P1) in Proposition~\ref{prop:smooth-decomposition-log-correlated-field}, we know that if $d_{\mathbb{T}^d}(\boldsymbol{z},\boldsymbol{z}')\ge 3\cdot 2^{-k}$, then \[ \mathbb{E}[X_k(\boldsymbol{z})X_k(\boldsymbol{z}')]=K_k(\boldsymbol{z}\cdot \overline{\boldsymbol{z}'})=0, \] that is, $X_k(\boldsymbol{z})$ and $X_k(\boldsymbol{z}')$ are independent. This proves (1).

nodes.name: (2) Count classes by an injection
nodes.statement: (2). Fix a cube $\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_{k,1}$, whose center $\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}}=(c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_d)$. Then for any $\mathscr{D}_{k,s}$, we can pick a unique cube $\boldsymbol{I}_s\in \mathscr{D}_{k,s}$, such that the center of $\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}_s}=(c_{s,1},c_{s,2},\ldots,c_{s,d})$ satisfying $c_{s,j}-c_{j}\in \{b\cdot 2^{-k}:b=0,1,\ldots,4\}$. In other words, the center of $\boldsymbol{I}_s$ can be written as \[ \boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}_s}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}}+2^{-k}\boldsymbol{b}_s, \] for some $\boldsymbol{b}_s=(b_{s,1},b_{s,2},\ldots,b_{s,d})\in \{0,1,2,3,4\}^d$. This gives an injection from $\{\mathscr{D}_{k,s}:s=1,2,\ldots,R_k\}$ to $\{0,1,2,3,4\}^d$, which provides us the upper bound of the number of partitions $S_k\le 5^d$.

nodes.name: Localization estimate
nodes.statement: For each $k\ge 1$ and $\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k$, we have the estimate \[ \mathbb{E}[\|\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\|_{\ell^q}^p]\lesssim k^{4dp} 2^{k(-dp+dp/q+\tau p/2)}\sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^k \big(\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]\big)\bigg]. \]
nodes.statement_short: Each localized FL piece has p-th moment <= k^{4dp} 2^{k(-dp+dp/q+tau p/2)} times the product of p-moments of X_j.
nodes.label: prop:localization

nodes.name: Limit of p-moments of X_j
nodes.statement: For any $0<p<\infty$, we have \[ \lim_{j\to \infty}\sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]=2^{p(p-1)\gamma^2/2}. \]
nodes.label: lemma:p-moment-Xj

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.5
nodes.statement: Fix $\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d$. We have \[ \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]=\mathbb{E}\big[\exp\big(p\gamma \psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\frac{p\gamma^2}{2}\mathbb{E}[\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})^2]\big)\big]=\exp\bigg(\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}\mathbb{E}[\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})^2]\bigg). \] Recalling that the kernel function of $\psi_j$ is $\mathcal{K}_j$, hence \[ \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]=\exp\bigg(\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}\mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{1})\bigg), \] which is independent of $\boldsymbol{z}$. Combining (P2) in Proposition~\ref{prop:smooth-decomposition-log-correlated-field}, we have \[ \lim_{j\to \infty}\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]=\lim_{j\to \infty}\exp\bigg(\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}\mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{1})\bigg)=\exp\bigg(\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}\log 2\bigg)=2^{p(p-1)\gamma^2/2}. \] This proves the desired limit.
nodes.statement_short: Compute the lognormal moment explicitly and use K_j(1) -> log 2.

nodes.name: Lognormal moment formula
nodes.statement: Fix $\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d$. We have \[ \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]=\mathbb{E}\big[\exp\big(p\gamma \psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\frac{p\gamma^2}{2}\mathbb{E}[\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})^2]\big)\big]=\exp\bigg(\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}\mathbb{E}[\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})^2]\bigg). \]

nodes.name: Substitute variance K_j(1)
nodes.statement: Recalling that the kernel function of $\psi_j$ is $\mathcal{K}_j$, hence \[ \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]=\exp\bigg(\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}\mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{1})\bigg), \] which is independent of $\boldsymbol{z}$.

nodes.name: Pass to the limit using K_j(1)->log 2
nodes.statement: Combining (P2) in Proposition~\ref{prop:smooth-decomposition-log-correlated-field}, we have \[ \lim_{j\to \infty}\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]=\lim_{j\to \infty}\exp\bigg(\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}\mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{1})\bigg)=\exp\bigg(\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}\log 2\bigg)=2^{p(p-1)\gamma^2/2}. \] This proves the desired limit.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to the limit using K_j(1)->log 2

nodes.name: Series bound for moments of M_m
nodes.statement: \notag \mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{M}_m\|_{\ell^q}^p]&\lesssim \sum_{k=1}^m k^{4dp} 2^{k(-(p-1)d+dp/q+\tau p/2)}\cdot 2^{kp(p-1)\gamma^2/2+\varepsilon}\\ &\lesssim \sum_{k=1}^\infty k^{4dp} 2^{k(-(p-1)d+dp/q+\tau p/2)}\cdot 2^{kp(p-1)\gamma^2/2+\varepsilon}.
nodes.label: eq:series-moment-estimate-Mm

nodes.name: Moments of higher derivatives of X_j
nodes.statement: For any $0<p<\infty$, we have \[ \sup_{j}\sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\frac{\mathbb{E}[|D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]}{j^{2|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|p}2^{j|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|p}}<\infty. \]
nodes.section: 4.2 Asymptotic estimates for the $p$-moments of derivatives of $X_j$
nodes.label: lemma:p-moment-higher-derivatives-Xj

nodes.name: Multivariate Faa di Bruno formula
nodes.statement: Let $U$ be a domain in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $f\in C^\infty(U)$. Then for any multi-index $\boldsymbol{\alpha}\in \mathbb{N}^d$, we have \[ \partial^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} e^f=e^f\sum_{\sum_\ell m_\ell \boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell=\boldsymbol{\alpha}} \frac{\boldsymbol{\alpha}!}{\prod_\ell m_\ell!}\prod_{\ell} \bigg(\frac{\partial^{\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell}f}{\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell!}\bigg)^{m_\ell}. \]
nodes.section: 4.2 Asymptotic estimates for the $p$-moments of derivatives of $X_j$
nodes.origin_citation: Faa di Bruno formula; Mouhot-Villani 2011, Appendix A.2
nodes.label: lemma:Faa-di-Bruno

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.6
nodes.statement: By definition, \[ D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} X_j(\boldsymbol{z})=D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\Big(\exp\big(\gamma \psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})-\frac{\gamma^2}{2}\mathbb{E}[\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})^2]\big)\Big)=\exp\big(\gamma^2 \mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{1})/2\big)\cdot D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\Big(\exp\big(\gamma\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})\big)\Big). \] By Lemma~\ref{lemma:Faa-di-Bruno}, we have \[ D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\exp\big(\gamma \psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})\big)=\exp(\gamma\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z}))\sum_{\sum_\ell m_\ell\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell=\boldsymbol{\alpha}} \frac{\boldsymbol{\alpha}!}{\prod_\ell m_\ell!} \prod_\ell \bigg(\frac{D^{\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell}\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})}{\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell!}\bigg)^{m_\ell}. \] Let $N(\boldsymbol{\alpha})$ denote the total number of unordered partitions $\sum_\ell m_\ell \boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell=\boldsymbol{\alpha}$. Then \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}[|D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]&=\mathbb{E}\bigg[\bigg|\exp(\gamma\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z}))\sum_{\sum_\ell m_\ell\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell=\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\frac{\boldsymbol{\alpha}!}{\prod_\ell m_\ell}\prod_\ell \bigg(\frac{D^{\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell}\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})}{\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell!}\bigg)^{m_\ell}\bigg|^p\bigg]\\ &\le N(\boldsymbol{\alpha})^{p-1}\sum_{\sum_\ell m_\ell \boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell=\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\frac{(\boldsymbol{\alpha}!)^p}{\prod_\ell (m_\ell!)^p} \mathbb{E}\bigg[\bigg|\exp(\gamma\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z}))\prod_{\ell} \bigg(\frac{D^{\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell}\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})}{\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell!}\bigg)^{m_\ell}\bigg|^p\bigg]. \end{align*} Applying the rough estimate $\prod_\ell m_\ell!\ge 1$ and $\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell!\ge 1$, we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}[|D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]&\le N(|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|)^p (\boldsymbol{\alpha}!)^p \sup_{\sum_\ell m_\ell \boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell=\boldsymbol{\alpha}} \mathbb{E}\bigg[\bigg|\exp(\gamma\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z}))\prod_{\ell} \bigg(\frac{D^{\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell}\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})}{\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell!}\bigg)^{m_\ell}\bigg|^p\bigg]\\ &\le N(|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|)^p (\boldsymbol{\alpha}!)^p \sup_{\sum_\ell m_\ell \boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell=\boldsymbol{\alpha}} \mathbb{E}\Big[\big|\exp(\gamma\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z}))\prod_{\ell} |D^{\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell}\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^{m_\ell}\big|^p\Big]. \end{align*} For each fixed unordered partition $\sum_\ell m_\ell \boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell=\boldsymbol{\alpha}$, we apply the generalized H\"{o}lder's inequality. Let $L$ be the number of distinct multi-indices $\{\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell\}_{\ell}$ in the partition. We make the specific choice \[ p_0 = p_\ell = (L+1)p \quad \text{for all } \ell. \] This choice of exponents satisfies the condition \[ \frac{1}{p_0} + \sum_{\ell} \frac{1}{p_\ell} = \frac{1}{p}. \] We then have \[ \mathbb{E}\Big[\big|\exp(\gamma\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z}))\prod_{\ell} |D^{\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell}\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^{m_\ell}\big|^p\Big]\le \mathbb{E}[\exp(p_0\gamma\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z}))]^{p/p_0}\cdot\prod_\ell \mathbb{E}[|D^{\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell}\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^{m_\ell p_\ell}]^{p/p_\ell}. \] Since $L$ can be bounded by $|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|$ and $p_0=(L+1)p$, we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}[\exp(p_0\gamma\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z}))]^{p/p_0}=\exp\Big(p_0p\gamma^2\mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{1})/2\Big)&=\exp\Big((L+1)p^2\gamma^2\mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{1})/2\Big)\\ &\le \exp\Big((|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|+1)p^2\gamma^2\mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{1})/2\Big). \end{align*} Additionally, we know that $\lim\limits_{j\to \infty}\mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{1})=\log 2$, so $\sup_j \mathcal{K}_j(\boldsymbol{1})\le C$ for some constant $C>0$. Thus \[ \mathbb{E}[\exp(p_0\gamma\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z}))]^{p/p_0}\le \exp\Big(C(|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|+1)p^2\gamma^2/2\Big). \] Now we estimate the product term $\prod_\ell \mathbb{E}[|D^{\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell}\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^{m_\ell p_\ell}]^{p/p_\ell}$. By (P4) in Proposition~\ref{prop:smooth-decomposition-log-correlated-field}, there exists an increasing function $\Theta$, such that \[ \mathbb{E}\big[|D^{\boldsymbol{\beta}_j}\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^{m_\ell p_\ell}\big]\le \Theta(m_\ell p_\ell) j^{2|\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell |m_\ell p_\ell}2^{j|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|m_\ell p_\ell}. \] Since $\sum_\ell m_\ell |\boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell|=|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|$, we have \[ \prod_{\ell}\Big(\mathbb{E}\big[\big|D^{\boldsymbol{\beta}_{\ell}}\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})\big|^{m_\ell p_\ell}\big]\Big)^{p/p_\ell}\le \bigg[\prod_\ell \Theta(m_\ell p_\ell)\bigg]^{p/p_\ell} j^{2|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|p}2^{j|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|p}. \] Therefore, \[ \frac{\mathbb{E}[|D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]}{j^{2|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|p}2^{j|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|p}}\le N(\boldsymbol{\alpha})^p(\boldsymbol{\alpha}!)^p\sup_{\sum_\ell m_\ell \boldsymbol{\beta}_\ell=\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\exp(p_0p\gamma^2\mathbb{E}[\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})^2]/2)\cdot\bigg[\prod_\ell \Theta(m_\ell p_\ell)\bigg]^{p/p_\ell}. \] Again, recalling that $p_\ell=(L+1)p\le (|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|+1)p$ and $m_\ell\le |\boldsymbol{\alpha}|$, we have \[ \prod_{\ell}\Big(\mathbb{E}\big[\big|D^{\boldsymbol{\beta}_{\ell}}\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})\big|^{m_\ell p_\ell}\big]\Big)^{p/p_\ell}\le \big(\Theta(|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|\cdot (|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|+1)p)\big)^{p\cdot \sum_\ell p_\ell^{-1}}j^{2|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|p}2^{j|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|p}, \] where we use the fact that $\Theta$ is increasing. Since $p\cdot \sum_{\ell}p_\ell^{-1}=p\cdot \frac{L}{(L+1)p}\le 1$ and $I\ge 1$, we have \[ \prod_{\ell}\Big(\mathbb{E}\big[\big|D^{\boldsymbol{\beta}_{\ell}}\psi_j(\boldsymbol{z})\big|^{m_\ell p_\ell}\big]\Big)^{p/p_\ell}\le \Theta(|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|\cdot (|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|+1)p)j^{2|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|p}2^{j|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|p}. \] Therefore, \[ \frac{\mathbb{E}[|D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]}{j^{2|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|p}2^{j|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|p}}\le N(\boldsymbol{\alpha})^p(\boldsymbol{\alpha}!)^p \exp\Big(C(|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|+1)p^2\gamma^2/2\Big)\cdot \Theta(|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|\cdot (|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|+1)p), \] where the right hand side of the inequality is a constant independent of $j$ and $\boldsymbol{z}$. This finishes our proof.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.4
nodes.statement:
To motivate the strategy of the forthcoming proof, we begin by discussing an one dimensional deterministic model example that explains the key analytic mechanism. { lushleft  f Heuristic.} Consider an oscillatory integral of the form \[ \int_I f(x) e^{2\pi i n x} \, \mathrm{d}x, \] where $I \subset \mathbb{R}$ is an interval of length $|I| = 2^{-k}$ and $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ denotes the frequency parameter. When $|n| \ll 2^k$, the exponential factor $e^{2\pi i n x}$ varies slowly over $I$ and can be regarded as approximately constant. In this regime, the integral is mainly determined by the average value of $f$ on $I$. In contrast, when $|n| \gg 2^k$, the rapid oscillations of $e^{2\pi i n x}$ within $I$ cause the integral to decay. In the high-frequency regime, the decay of the integral can be effectively estimated by repeated integration by parts, which is a standard technique for oscillatory integrals. Recall that \[ \mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{n})=\langle  oldsymbol{n}angle^{	au/2}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\varphi_{ oldsymbol{I}}( oldsymbol{z}) igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j( oldsymbol{z}) igg]\mathring{X}_k( oldsymbol{z})\cdot  oldsymbol{z}^{ oldsymbol{n}}\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{z}, \] where $\mathring{X}_k( oldsymbol{z})=X_k( oldsymbol{z})-1, orall  oldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d$. For simplicity of our analysis, we can bound the centered process $\mathring{X}_k$ by the original process $X_k$. The validity of this approach, up to a multiplicative constant, is justified by the following lemma.  egin{lemma} Let $k\ge 1$ be integer. For any $1\le p<\infty$, there exists a constant $C(p)>0$ depending only on $p$, such that \[ \mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\le C(p)\mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}X_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]. \] \end{lemma}  egin{proof} Let $ oldsymbol{\alpha}\in \mathbb{N}^d$ be a multi-index.  egin{itemize} \item If $ oldsymbol{\alpha}
e  oldsymbol{0}$, then \[ (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))=(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}X_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})). \] In this case, the equality \[ \mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]=\mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}X_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] \] holds. \item If $ oldsymbol{\alpha}= oldsymbol{0}$, then \[ \mathbb{E}[|\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]=\mathbb{E}[|X_k(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))-1|^p]\le 2^{p-1} ig(\mathbb{E}[|X_k(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]+1 ig). \] For $1\le p<\infty$, we have \[ \mathbb{E}[|X_k(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]=\exp ig( rac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}K_k( oldsymbol{1}) ig)\ge 1. \] Thus \[ \mathbb{E}[|\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\le 2^{p-1}\cdot 2\mathbb{E}[|X_k(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]=2^p\mathbb{E}[|X_k(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]. \] \end{itemize} If we define $C(p)=2^{p}, orall p\ge 1$, then for any $1\le p<\infty$, \[ \mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\le C(p)\mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}X_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p], \] which proves this lemma. \end{proof} \subsubsection{High-low frequency decomposition} Firstly, we divide $\mathbb{E}[\|\mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\|_{\ell^q}^p]$ into low frequency and high frequency parts. Since $q/p\le 1$, we have  egin{align*} \mathbb{E}[\|\mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\|_{\ell^q}^p]&=\mathbb{E} igg[ igg\{\sum_{ oldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d} |\mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi ( oldsymbol{n})|^q igg\}^{p/q} igg]\ &\le \mathbb{E} igg[ igg\{\sum_{\substack{ oldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d,\| oldsymbol{n}|\le 2^k}} |\mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi ( oldsymbol{n})|^q igg\}^{p/q} igg]+\mathbb{E} igg[ igg\{\sum_{\substack{ oldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d,\| oldsymbol{n}|>2^k}} |\mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi ( oldsymbol{n})|^q igg\}^{p/q} igg]\ &=I_{	extnormal{low}}+I_{	extnormal{high}}. \end{align*} \subsubsection{Bound $I_{	extnormal{low}}$} Since the oscillation is negligible in this case, we can simply bound $|\mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{n})|$ by \[ |\mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{n})|\le \langle  oldsymbol{n}angle^{	au/2}\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d}  igg|\varphi_{ oldsymbol{I}}(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t})) igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t})) igg]\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t})) igg|\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}. \] Note that the integral term is independent of $ oldsymbol{n}$, hence we can take it out of the summation over $ oldsymbol{n}$. Therefore,  egin{align*} \sum_{\substack{ oldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d,\| oldsymbol{n}|\le 2^k}} |\mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi ( oldsymbol{n})|^q&\le  igg\{\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d}  igg|\varphi_{ oldsymbol{I}}(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t})) igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t})) igg]\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t})) igg|\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t} igg\}^q\cdot  igg\{\sum_{\substack{ oldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z},\| oldsymbol{n}|\le 2^k}} \langle  oldsymbol{n}angle^{	au q/2} igg\}\ &\lesssim 2^{k	au q/2}\cdot 2^{kd}\cdot  igg\{\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d}  igg|\varphi_{ oldsymbol{I}}(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t})) igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t})) igg]\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t})) igg|\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t} igg\}^q. \end{align*} It follows that  egin{align*} I_{	extnormal{low}}&\lesssim 2^{k	au p/2}\cdot 2^{kdp/q}\cdot \mathbb{E} igg[ igg\{\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d}  igg|\varphi_{ oldsymbol{I}}(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t})) igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t})) igg]\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t})) igg|\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t} igg\}^p igg]\ &\le 2^{k(	au p/2+dp/q)}\cdot  igg\{\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d} |\varphi_{ oldsymbol{I}}(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}))| igg\{\mathbb{E} igg[ igg| igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t})) igg]\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t})) igg|^p igg] igg\}^{1/p}\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t} igg\}^p, \end{align*} where the second inequality holds by Minkowski's inequality. Since $\varphi_{ oldsymbol{I}}$ is supported on $2^{-k}([-1,1)^d+ oldsymbol{c_I})$, which has volume $2^{-(k-1)d}$, we have \[ I_{	extnormal{low}}\lesssim 2^{k(-dp+	au p/2+dp/q)}\cdot \sup_{ oldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\mathbb{E} igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} |X_j( oldsymbol{z})|^p |\mathring{X}_k( oldsymbol{z})|^p igg]. \] Using the independence of $X_j$'s and Lemma~ef{lemma:substitue-Xk-ring}, we obtain  egin{equation} I_{	extnormal{low}}\lesssim 2^{k(-dp+	au p/2+dp/q)}\cdot \sup_{ oldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d} igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k}\mathbb{E}[|X_j( oldsymbol{z})|^p] igg]. \end{equation} \subsubsection{Bound $I_{	extnormal{high}}$} We will divide the estimate of $I_{	extnormal{high}}$ into two steps for clarity. \medskip { lushleft  f Step 1. Integration by parts.} \medskip Our main goal in bounding $I_{	extnormal{high}}$ is to exploit the rapid oscillation of the term $e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{t})$ for large $| oldsymbol{n}|$. As mentioned earlier, the standard analytical tool for estimating such oscillatory integrals is integration by parts. In our multi-dimensional setting, this is achieved via Green's second identity.  egin{lemma}[Green's second identity] Let $\Omega$ be a region in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and let $f,g\in C^\infty(\Omega)$. We have  egin{equation} \int_{\Omega}(\Delta f)\cdot g\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}=\int_{\Omega} f\cdot (\Delta g)\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}+\int_{\partial \Omega}  igg( rac{\partial f}{\partial  oldsymbol{n}}\cdot g-f\cdot  rac{\partial g}{\partial  oldsymbol{n}} igg)\,\mathrm{d}\sigma, \end{equation} where $ rac{\partial f}{\partial  oldsymbol{n}}$ is the normal derivative of $f$ on the boundary $\partial \Omega$ and $\mathrm{d}\sigma$ is the surface measure on $\partial \Omega$. \end{lemma} Note that \[ \Delta e_{ oldsymbol{n}}=-4\pi^2| oldsymbol{n}|^2e_{ oldsymbol{n}}. \] If $f$ is a $C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$ function supported on $\Omega$, then the boundary term in \eqref{eq:Green's-second-id} vanishes.
