nodes.statement_short: High-low frequency split: low frequencies bounded trivially, high frequencies by d-fold integration by parts via Green's identity. The key step bounds moments of 2d-th derivatives of the localized product (Lemma 4.11).

nodes.name: Heuristic: low vs high frequency behaviour
nodes.statement: To motivate the strategy of the forthcoming proof, we begin by discussing an one dimensional deterministic model example that explains the key analytic mechanism. {\flushleft \bf Heuristic.} Consider an oscillatory integral of the form \[ \int_I f(x) e^{2\pi i n x} \, \mathrm{d}x, \] where $I \subset \mathbb{R}$ is an interval of length $|I| = 2^{-k}$ and $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ denotes the frequency parameter. When $|n| \ll 2^k$, the exponential factor $e^{2\pi i n x}$ varies slowly over $I$ and can be regarded as approximately constant. In this regime, the integral is mainly determined by the average value of $f$ on $I$. In contrast, when $|n| \gg 2^k$, the rapid oscillations of $e^{2\pi i n x}$ within $I$ cause the integral to decay. In the high-frequency regime, the decay of the integral can be effectively estimated by repeated integration by parts, which is a standard technique for oscillatory integrals.
nodes.statement_short: Heuristic: low vs high frequency behaviour

nodes.name: Replace centered X_k by X_k (Lemma 4.8)
nodes.statement: Recall that \[ \mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n})=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}(\boldsymbol{z})\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\boldsymbol{z})\cdot \boldsymbol{z}^{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z}, \] where $\mathring{X}_k(\boldsymbol{z})=X_k(\boldsymbol{z})-1,\forall \boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d$. For simplicity of our analysis, we can bound the centered process $\mathring{X}_k$ by the original process $X_k$. The validity of this approach, up to a multiplicative constant, is justified by the following lemma. \begin{lemma} Let $k\ge 1$ be integer. For any $1\le p<\infty$, there exists a constant $C(p)>0$ depending only on $p$, such that \[ \mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\le C(p)\mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}X_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]. \] \end{lemma} \begin{proof} Let $\boldsymbol{\alpha}\in \mathbb{N}^d$ be a multi-index. \begin{itemize} \item If $\boldsymbol{\alpha}\ne \boldsymbol{0}$, then \[ (D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))=(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}X_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I})). \] In this case, the equality \[ \mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]=\mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}X_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] \] holds. \item If $\boldsymbol{\alpha}=\boldsymbol{0}$, then \[ \mathbb{E}[|\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]=\mathbb{E}[|X_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))-1|^p]\le 2^{p-1}\big(\mathbb{E}[|X_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]+1\big). \] For $1\le p<\infty$, we have \[ \mathbb{E}[|X_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]=\exp\big(\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}K_k(\boldsymbol{1})\big)\ge 1. \] Thus \[ \mathbb{E}[|\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\le 2^{p-1}\cdot 2\mathbb{E}[|X_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]=2^p\mathbb{E}[|X_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]. \] \end{itemize} If we define $C(p)=2^{p},\forall p\ge 1$, then for any $1\le p<\infty$, \[ \mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\le C(p)\mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}X_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p], \] which proves this lemma. \end{proof}

nodes.name: Split into low and high frequency parts
nodes.statement: Firstly, we divide $\mathbb{E}[\|\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\|_{\ell^q}^p]$ into low frequency and high frequency parts. Since $q/p\le 1$, we have \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}[\|\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\|_{\ell^q}^p]&=\mathbb{E}\bigg[\bigg\{\sum_{\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d} |\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi (\boldsymbol{n})|^q\bigg\}^{p/q}\bigg]\\ &\le \mathbb{E}\bigg[\bigg\{\sum_{\substack{\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d,\\|\boldsymbol{n}|\le 2^k}} |\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi (\boldsymbol{n})|^q\bigg\}^{p/q}\bigg]+\mathbb{E}\bigg[\bigg\{\sum_{\substack{\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d,\\|\boldsymbol{n}|>2^k}} |\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi (\boldsymbol{n})|^q\bigg\}^{p/q}\bigg]\\ &=I_{\textnormal{low}}+I_{\textnormal{high}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Split into low and high frequency parts

nodes.name: Bound I_low trivially
nodes.statement: Since the oscillation is negligible in this case, we can simply bound $|\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n})|$ by \[ |\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n})|\le \langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d} \bigg|\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg|\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}. \] Note that the integral term is independent of $\boldsymbol{n}$, hence we can take it out of the summation over $\boldsymbol{n}$. Therefore, \begin{align*} \sum_{\substack{\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d,\\|\boldsymbol{n}|\le 2^k}} |\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi (\boldsymbol{n})|^q&\le \bigg\{\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d} \bigg|\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg|\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\bigg\}^q\cdot \bigg\{\sum_{\substack{\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z},\\|\boldsymbol{n}|\le 2^k}} \langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau q/2}\bigg\}\\ &\lesssim 2^{k\tau q/2}\cdot 2^{kd}\cdot \bigg\{\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d} \bigg|\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg|\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\bigg\}^q. \end{align*} It follows that \begin{align*} I_{\textnormal{low}}&\lesssim 2^{k\tau p/2}\cdot 2^{kdp/q}\cdot \mathbb{E}\bigg[\bigg\{\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d} \bigg|\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg|\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\bigg\}^p\bigg]\\ &\le 2^{k(\tau p/2+dp/q)}\cdot \bigg\{\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d} |\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))|\bigg\{\mathbb{E}\bigg[\bigg|\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg|^p\bigg]\bigg\}^{1/p}\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\bigg\}^p, \end{align*} where the second inequality holds by Minkowski's inequality. Since $\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}$ is supported on $2^{-k}([-1,1)^d+\boldsymbol{c_I})$, which has volume $2^{-(k-1)d}$, we have \[ I_{\textnormal{low}}\lesssim 2^{k(-dp+\tau p/2+dp/q)}\cdot \sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\mathbb{E}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} |X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p |\mathring{X}_k(\boldsymbol{z})|^p\bigg]. \] Using the independence of $X_j$'s and Lemma~\ref{lemma:substitue-Xk-ring}, we obtain \begin{equation} I_{\textnormal{low}}\lesssim 2^{k(-dp+\tau p/2+dp/q)}\cdot \sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k}\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]\bigg]. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Bound I_high by integration by parts
nodes.statement:
We will divide the estimate of $I_{	extnormal{high}}$ into two steps for clarity. \medskip { lushleft  f Step 1. Integration by parts.} \medskip Our main goal in bounding $I_{	extnormal{high}}$ is to exploit the rapid oscillation of the term $e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{t})$ for large $| oldsymbol{n}|$. As mentioned earlier, the standard analytical tool for estimating such oscillatory integrals is integration by parts. In our multi-dimensional setting, this is achieved via Green's second identity.  egin{lemma}[Green's second identity] Let $\Omega$ be a region in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and let $f,g\in C^\infty(\Omega)$. We have  egin{equation} \int_{\Omega}(\Delta f)\cdot g\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}=\int_{\Omega} f\cdot (\Delta g)\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}+\int_{\partial \Omega}  igg( rac{\partial f}{\partial  oldsymbol{n}}\cdot g-f\cdot  rac{\partial g}{\partial  oldsymbol{n}} igg)\,\mathrm{d}\sigma, \end{equation} where $ rac{\partial f}{\partial  oldsymbol{n}}$ is the normal derivative of $f$ on the boundary $\partial \Omega$ and $\mathrm{d}\sigma$ is the surface measure on $\partial \Omega$. \end{lemma} Note that \[ \Delta e_{ oldsymbol{n}}=-4\pi^2| oldsymbol{n}|^2e_{ oldsymbol{n}}. \] If $f$ is a $C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$ function supported on $\Omega$, then the boundary term in \eqref{eq:Green's-second-id} vanishes. In this case, we have  egin{equation} \int_{\Omega}(\Delta f)( oldsymbol{t})\cdot e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}=\int_\Omega f( oldsymbol{t})\Delta e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}=-4\pi^2| oldsymbol{n}|^2\int_{\Omega} f( oldsymbol{t})e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}. \end{equation} For each $k\ge 1$ and $ oldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k$, define the function $\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\colon \mathbb{R}^d	o \mathbb{R}$ by \[ \mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{t})\coloneq \varphi_k(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t})) igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg]\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})),\quad  orall  oldsymbol{t}\in [-1/2,1/2]^d, \] and extend it to $\mathbb{R}^d$ by zero. Then $\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi$ is a $C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$ function supported on $2^{-k}[-1,1)^d$.  egin{lemma} Let $	au>0$. For each $k\ge 1$, $ oldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k$ and $ oldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d\setminus\{ oldsymbol{0}\}$, we have \[ \mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{n})=\langle  oldsymbol{n}angle^{	au/2}e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{c}_{ oldsymbol{I}})(-4\pi^2| oldsymbol{n}|^2)^{-d}\sum_{| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}(\partial^{2 oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)( oldsymbol{t})e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}. \] \end{lemma}  egin{proof} Note that  egin{align*} \mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{n})&=\langle  oldsymbol{n}angle^{	au/2}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\varphi_{ oldsymbol{I}}( oldsymbol{z})  igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j( oldsymbol{z}) igg]\mathring{X}_k( oldsymbol{z})\cdot  oldsymbol{z}^{ oldsymbol{n}}\, oldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{z})\ &=\langle  oldsymbol{n}angle^{	au/2}\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d}\varphi_{ oldsymbol{I}}(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t})) igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t})) igg] \mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}))\cdot e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}\ &=\langle  oldsymbol{n}angle^{	au/2}\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d+ oldsymbol{c_I}}\varphi_{k}(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}- oldsymbol{c_I})) igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t})) igg] \mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}))\cdot e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}. \end{align*} By changing of variables, we have  egin{align*} \mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{n})&=\langle  oldsymbol{n}angle^{	au/2}e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{c}_{ oldsymbol{I}})\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d}\varphi_{k}(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}))  igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg] \mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))\cdot e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}\ &=\langle  oldsymbol{n}angle^{	au/2}e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{c}_{ oldsymbol{I}})\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{t})e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}. \end{align*} Applying \eqref{eq:Green's-second-id-2}, one can obtain \[ \int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{t})e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}=(-4\pi^2 | oldsymbol{n}|^2)^{-d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}(\Delta^d\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)( oldsymbol{t}) e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}. \] Therefore  egin{align*} \mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{n})&=\langle  oldsymbol{n}angle^{	au/2}e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{c}_{ oldsymbol{I}})(-4\pi^2| oldsymbol{n}|^2)^{-d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}(\Delta^d\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)( oldsymbol{t})e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}\ &=\langle  oldsymbol{n}angle^{	au/2}e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{c}_{ oldsymbol{I}})(-4\pi^2| oldsymbol{n}|^2)^{-d}\sum_{| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}(\partial^{2 oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)( oldsymbol{t})e_{ oldsymbol{n}}( oldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}. \end{align*} This completes the proof of this lemma. \end{proof} \medskip { lushleft  f Step 2. Bound the integral term.} \medskip By Lemma~ef{lemma:integration-by-parts}, for $ oldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d\setminus\{ oldsymbol{0}\}$, we have  egin{align*} |\mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{n})|&\le \langle  oldsymbol{n}angle^{	au/2}(4\pi^2| oldsymbol{n}|^2)^{-d}\sum_{| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d} ig|(\partial^{2 oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)( oldsymbol{t}) ig|\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}\ &\lesssim | oldsymbol{n}|^{	au/2-2d}\cdot \sum_{| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d} ig|(\partial^{2 oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)( oldsymbol{t}) ig|\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}. \end{align*} Again, observe that the integral term does not depend on $ oldsymbol{n}$, so it can be factored out of the summation over $ oldsymbol{n}$, yielding \[ \sum_{\substack{ oldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d,\| oldsymbol{n}|>2^k}} |\mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi ( oldsymbol{n})|^q\lesssim  igg\{\sum_{\substack{ oldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d,\| oldsymbol{n}|>2^k}}| oldsymbol{n}|^{(	au/2-2d)q} igg\}\cdot  igg(\sum_{| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d} ig|(\partial^{2 oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)( oldsymbol{t}) ig|\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t} igg)^q. \] The series about $ oldsymbol{n}$ converges for $	au<4d$ and sufficiently large $q$, which can be bounded by $2^{k(	au q/2-2dq+d)}$. Therefore, we have  egin{align*}  igg\{\sum_{\substack{ oldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d,\| oldsymbol{n}|>2^k}} |\mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{n})|^q igg\}^{p/q}\lesssim 2^{k(	au p/2-2dp+dp/q)}\cdot  igg(\sum_{| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d} ig|(\partial^{2 oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)( oldsymbol{t}) ig|\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t} igg)^p. \end{align*} Thus, applying Minkowski's inequality, we obtain  egin{align*} I_{	extnormal{high}}=\mathbb{E} igg[ igg\{\sum_{\substack{ oldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d,\| oldsymbol{n}|>2^k}} |\mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{n})|^q igg\}^{p/q} igg]&\lesssim 2^{k(	au p/2-2dp+dp/q)} igg\{\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d} \sum_{| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=d} ig(\mathbb{E}[|(\partial^{2 oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)( oldsymbol{t})|^p] ig)^{1/p}\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t} igg\}^p\ &\lesssim 2^{k(	au p/2-2dp+dp/q)}\cdot 2^{-kdp}\cdot \sup_{| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=2d}\sup_{ oldsymbol{t}\in 2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}\mathbb{E}[|\partial^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{t})|^p]. \end{align*} The following lemma provides a bound for the $p$-norm of the higher derivatives of $\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi$.  egin{lemma} For any $1\le p<\infty$, and any integer $A\ge 0$, we have \[ \sup_{| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=A}\sup_{ oldsymbol{t}\in 2^{-k}[-1,1)^d} ig(\mathbb{E}[|\partial^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{t})|^p] ig)^{1/p}\lesssim \sup_{ oldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d} igg[\prod_{1\le j\le k} ig(\mathbb{E}[|D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}X_j( oldsymbol{z})|^p] ig)^{1/p} igg]\cdot (k^2 2^k)^{A}, \] where the implicit constant is independent of $k$ and $ oldsymbol{I}$. \end{lemma} Taking $A=2d$ in this lemma, we can conclude that  egin{equation} I_{	extnormal{high}}\lesssim k^{4dp}\cdot 2^{k(-dp+	au p/2+dp/q)}\cdot \sup_{ oldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d} igg[\prod_{1\le j\le k}\mathbb{E}[|D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}X_j( oldsymbol{z})|^p] igg]. \end{equation} Now we turn back to prove Lemma~ef{lemma:p-norm-h-derivatives-of-XIphi}.  egin{proof}[Proof of Lemma~ef{lemma:p-norm-h-derivatives-of-XIphi}] Since $\partial_\ell$ commutes with translation, we know that \[ (\partial^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\cdot+ oldsymbol{c_I})))( oldsymbol{t})=(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})). \] The same formula holds for $\mathring{X}_k$. Therefore, for a multi-index $ oldsymbol{\alpha}$ with $| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=R$, by Leibniz rule, we have \[ \partial^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{t})=\sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{\alpha}}  rac{ oldsymbol{\alpha}!}{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0! oldsymbol{\alpha}_1!\cdots  oldsymbol{\alpha}_k!}(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0} \varphi_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}))\cdot  igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg]\cdot (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})), \] where we write $ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j=(\alpha_{j,1},\alpha_{j,2},\ldots,\alpha_{j,d})$ and $ oldsymbol{\alpha}=(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\ldots,\alpha_d)$. For clarity, we emphasize that bold symbols such as $ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j$ denote multi-indices, while non-bold symbols like $\alpha_j$ represent scalar components. To bound this sum, our strategy is to estimate each term by applying independence to separate the products, bounding the moments of each derivative factor using Lemma~ef{lemma:p-moment-higher-derivatives-Xj} and Lemma~ef{lemma:pou-scaling-Td}, and finally resumming the bounds via the multinomial theorem. Let $\sum_{j=0}^k  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{\alpha}$ be a fixed partition. By Lemma~ef{lemma:substitue-Xk-ring} and independence of $X_j$'s, we have  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E} igg[ igg|  igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg]\cdot (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg|^p igg]\ &= igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}\mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\cdot \mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] \ & \lesssim \prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]. \end{align*} Since $\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\ge 1$, we can insert at most $R$ terms $X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))$ with $ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{0}$, which gives  egin{align*} \prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]&= igg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j
e  oldsymbol{0}}}\mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\cdot  igg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{0}}}\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\ &\le  igg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j
e 0}} \mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\cdot igg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]. \end{align*} By Lemma~ef{lemma:p-moment-higher-derivatives-Xj}, for each $1\le j\le k$, there exists a constant $M(p, oldsymbol{\alpha}_j)>0$ such that \[ \mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\le M(p, oldsymbol{\alpha}_j) j^{2| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}. \] By Lemma~ef{lemma:pou-scaling-Td}, we have \[ \|D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0}\varphi_k\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^d)}\lesssim 2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|}. \] Thereofre,  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E} igg[ igg|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0} \varphi_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}))\cdot  igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg]\cdot (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg|^p igg]\ &\lesssim 2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|p} igg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\cdot igg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j
e 0}}(M(p, oldsymbol{\alpha}_j)j^{2| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}) igg]. \end{align*} Since the number of non-zero $\alpha_j$ in $\sum_j  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{\alpha}$ is not larger than $A$, we have  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E} igg[ igg|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0} \varphi_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}))\cdot  igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg]\cdot (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg|^p igg]\ &\lesssim 2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|p} igg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\cdot igg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j
e 0}}(M(p, oldsymbol{\alpha}_j)j^{2| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}) igg]. \end{align*} Since the number of non-zero $\alpha_j$ in $\sum_j  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{\alpha}$ is not larger than $A$, we have  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E} igg[ igg|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0} \varphi_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}))\cdot  igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg]\cdot (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg|^p igg]\ &\lesssim \max\Big\{\sup_{| oldsymbol{ eta}|\le A}M(p, oldsymbol{ eta})^A,1\Big\} \cdot  igg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\cdot 2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|p} igg[ \prod_{1\le j\le k} j^{2| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p} igg]\ &\lesssim \sup_{ oldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d} igg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j( oldsymbol{z})|^p] igg]\cdot 2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|p} igg[\prod_{1\le j\le k} j^{2| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p} igg]. \end{align*} By Minkowski inequality, we have  egin{align*} &\quad \, ig(\mathbb{E}[|\partial^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{t})|^p] ig)^{1/p}\ &\lesssim \sup_{ oldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d} igg[\prod_{j=1}^k (\mathbb{E}[|X_j( oldsymbol{z})|^p])^{1/p} igg]\cdot  igg\{\sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{\alpha}} rac{ oldsymbol{\alpha}!}{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0! oldsymbol{\alpha}_1!\cdots  oldsymbol{\alpha}_k!}  igg(2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|}\prod_{1\le j\le k} (j^2 2^j)^{| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|} igg) igg\}. \end{align*} Note that by the definition of the factorial of a multi-index and the separability of the products, the sum can be decomposed over each dimension $\ell=1,\ldots,d$:  egin{align*} \sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{\alpha}} rac{ oldsymbol{\alpha}!}{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0!\cdots  oldsymbol{\alpha}_k!} igg(2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|}\prod_{1\le j\le k} (j^2 2^j)^{| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|} igg)=\prod_{\ell=1}^d \Bigg\{ \sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k \alpha_{j,\ell}=\alpha_\ell} rac{\alpha_\ell!}{\alpha_{0,\ell}!\cdots \alpha_{k,\ell}!} 2^{k\alpha_{0,\ell}} \prod_{1\le j\le k} (j^2 2^j)^{\alpha_{j,\ell}} \Bigg\}. \end{align*} The inner sum for each $\ell$ is now a direct application of the multinomial theorem:  egin{align*} \sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k \alpha_{j,\ell}=\alpha_\ell} rac{\alpha_\ell!}{\alpha_{0,\ell}!\cdots \alpha_{k,\ell}!} 2^{k\alpha_{0,\ell}} \prod_{1\le j\le k} (j^2 2^j)^{\alpha_{j,\ell}} = \left(2^k+\sum_{j=1}^k j^2 2^jight)^{\alpha_\ell}. \end{align*} Substituting this back and combining the exponents, we conclude that  egin{equation*} \left(2^k+\sum_{j=1}^k j^2 2^jight)^{\sum_{\ell=1}^d \alpha_\ell} = \left(2^k+\sum_{j=1}^k j^2 2^jight)^{A}. \end{equation*} Since \[ 2^k+\sum_{j=1}^k j^2 2^j\le 2^k+k^2\sum_{j=0}^k 2^j=2^k+k^2(2^{k+1}-1)\le 3k^2 2^k, \] we conclude that \[  ig(\mathbb{E}[|\partial^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{t})|^p] ig)^{1/p}\lesssim \sup_{ oldsymbol{z}\in T^d} igg[\prod_{j=1}^k (\mathbb{E}[|X_j( oldsymbol{z})|^p])^{1/p} igg]\cdot (k^22^k)^A. \] Taking supremum over $ oldsymbol{t}\in 2^{-k}[-1,1)^d$, we finish the proof. \end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Bound I_high by integration by parts

nodes.name: Combine low and high bounds
nodes.statement: We combine the bounds \eqref{eq:bound-I-low} and \eqref{eq:bound-I-high} to obtain \[ \mathbb{E}[\|\mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\|_{\ell^q}^p]\lesssim k^{4dp}\cdot 2^{k(-dp+\tau p/2+dp/q)}\cdot \sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]\bigg]. \] This proves Proposition~\ref{prop:localization}.

nodes.name: Announce two steps
nodes.statement: We will divide the estimate of $I_{\textnormal{high}}$ into two steps for clarity.

nodes.name: Step 1
nodes.statement: {\flushleft \bf Step 1. Integration by parts.} \medskip Our main goal in bounding $I_{\textnormal{high}}$ is to exploit the rapid oscillation of the term $e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})$ for large $|\boldsymbol{n}|$. As mentioned earlier, the standard analytical tool for estimating such oscillatory integrals is integration by parts. In our multi-dimensional setting, this is achieved via Green's second identity. \begin{lemma}[Green's second identity] Let $\Omega$ be a region in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and let $f,g\in C^\infty(\Omega)$. We have \begin{equation} \int_{\Omega}(\Delta f)\cdot g\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}=\int_{\Omega} f\cdot (\Delta g)\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}+\int_{\partial \Omega} \bigg(\frac{\partial f}{\partial \boldsymbol{n}}\cdot g-f\cdot \frac{\partial g}{\partial \boldsymbol{n}}\bigg)\,\mathrm{d}\sigma, \end{equation} where $\frac{\partial f}{\partial \boldsymbol{n}}$ is the normal derivative of $f$ on the boundary $\partial \Omega$ and $\mathrm{d}\sigma$ is the surface measure on $\partial \Omega$. \end{lemma} Note that \[ \Delta e_{\boldsymbol{n}}=-4\pi^2|\boldsymbol{n}|^2e_{\boldsymbol{n}}. \] If $f$ is a $C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$ function supported on $\Omega$, then the boundary term in \eqref{eq:Green's-second-id} vanishes. In this case, we have \begin{equation} \int_{\Omega}(\Delta f)(\boldsymbol{t})\cdot e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}=\int_\Omega f(\boldsymbol{t})\Delta e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}=-4\pi^2|\boldsymbol{n}|^2\int_{\Omega} f(\boldsymbol{t})e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}. \end{equation} For each $k\ge 1$ and $\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k$, define the function $\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi\colon \mathbb{R}^d\to \mathbb{R}$ by \[ \mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{t})\coloneq \varphi_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I})),\quad \forall \boldsymbol{t}\in [-1/2,1/2]^d, \] and extend it to $\mathbb{R}^d$ by zero. Then $\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi$ is a $C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$ function supported on $2^{-k}[-1,1)^d$. \begin{lemma} Let $\tau>0$. For each $k\ge 1$, $\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k$ and $\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d\setminus\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$, we have \[ \mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n})=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}})(-4\pi^2|\boldsymbol{n}|^2)^{-d}\sum_{|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|=d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}(\partial^{2\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)(\boldsymbol{t})e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}. \] \end{lemma} \begin{proof} Note that \begin{align*} \mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n})&=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}(\boldsymbol{z}) \bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\boldsymbol{z})\cdot \boldsymbol{z}^{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z})\\ &=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d}\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg] \mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\cdot e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\\ &=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d+\boldsymbol{c_I}}\varphi_{k}(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}-\boldsymbol{c_I}))\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg] \mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\cdot e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}. \end{align*} By changing of variables, we have \begin{align*} \mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n})&=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}})\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d}\varphi_{k}(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t})) \bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))\bigg] \mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))\cdot e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\\ &=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}})\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{t})e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}. \end{align*} Applying \eqref{eq:Green's-second-id-2}, one can obtain \[ \int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{t})e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}=(-4\pi^2 |\boldsymbol{n}|^2)^{-d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}(\Delta^d\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)(\boldsymbol{t}) e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}. \] Therefore \begin{align*} \mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n})&=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}})(-4\pi^2|\boldsymbol{n}|^2)^{-d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}(\Delta^d\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)(\boldsymbol{t})e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\\ &=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}})(-4\pi^2|\boldsymbol{n}|^2)^{-d}\sum_{|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|=d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}(\partial^{2\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)(\boldsymbol{t})e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}. \end{align*} This completes the proof of this lemma. \end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Step 1: integration by parts via Green's identity

nodes.name: Step 2
nodes.statement:
{ lushleft  f Step 2. Bound the integral term.} \medskip By Lemma~ef{lemma:integration-by-parts}, for $ oldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d\setminus\{ oldsymbol{0}\}$, we have  egin{align*} |\mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{n})|&\le \langle  oldsymbol{n}angle^{	au/2}(4\pi^2| oldsymbol{n}|^2)^{-d}\sum_{| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d} ig|(\partial^{2 oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)( oldsymbol{t}) ig|\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}\ &\lesssim | oldsymbol{n}|^{	au/2-2d}\cdot \sum_{| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d} ig|(\partial^{2 oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)( oldsymbol{t}) ig|\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t}. \end{align*} Again, observe that the integral term does not depend on $ oldsymbol{n}$, so it can be factored out of the summation over $ oldsymbol{n}$, yielding \[ \sum_{\substack{ oldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d,\| oldsymbol{n}|>2^k}} |\mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi ( oldsymbol{n})|^q\lesssim  igg\{\sum_{\substack{ oldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d,\| oldsymbol{n}|>2^k}}| oldsymbol{n}|^{(	au/2-2d)q} igg\}\cdot  igg(\sum_{| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d} ig|(\partial^{2 oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)( oldsymbol{t}) ig|\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t} igg)^q. \] The series about $ oldsymbol{n}$ converges for $	au<4d$ and sufficiently large $q$, which can be bounded by $2^{k(	au q/2-2dq+d)}$. Therefore, we have  egin{align*}  igg\{\sum_{\substack{ oldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d,\| oldsymbol{n}|>2^k}} |\mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{n})|^q igg\}^{p/q}\lesssim 2^{k(	au p/2-2dp+dp/q)}\cdot  igg(\sum_{| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d} ig|(\partial^{2 oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)( oldsymbol{t}) ig|\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t} igg)^p. \end{align*} Thus, applying Minkowski's inequality, we obtain  egin{align*} I_{	extnormal{high}}=\mathbb{E} igg[ igg\{\sum_{\substack{ oldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d,\| oldsymbol{n}|>2^k}} |\mathfrak{D}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{n})|^q igg\}^{p/q} igg]&\lesssim 2^{k(	au p/2-2dp+dp/q)} igg\{\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d} \sum_{| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=d} ig(\mathbb{E}[|(\partial^{2 oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)( oldsymbol{t})|^p] ig)^{1/p}\,\mathrm{d} oldsymbol{t} igg\}^p\ &\lesssim 2^{k(	au p/2-2dp+dp/q)}\cdot 2^{-kdp}\cdot \sup_{| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=2d}\sup_{ oldsymbol{t}\in 2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}\mathbb{E}[|\partial^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{t})|^p]. \end{align*} The following lemma provides a bound for the $p$-norm of the higher derivatives of $\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi$.  egin{lemma} For any $1\le p<\infty$, and any integer $A\ge 0$, we have \[ \sup_{| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=A}\sup_{ oldsymbol{t}\in 2^{-k}[-1,1)^d} ig(\mathbb{E}[|\partial^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{t})|^p] ig)^{1/p}\lesssim \sup_{ oldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d} igg[\prod_{1\le j\le k} ig(\mathbb{E}[|D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}X_j( oldsymbol{z})|^p] ig)^{1/p} igg]\cdot (k^2 2^k)^{A}, \] where the implicit constant is independent of $k$ and $ oldsymbol{I}$. \end{lemma} Taking $A=2d$ in this lemma, we can conclude that  egin{equation} I_{	extnormal{high}}\lesssim k^{4dp}\cdot 2^{k(-dp+	au p/2+dp/q)}\cdot \sup_{ oldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d} igg[\prod_{1\le j\le k}\mathbb{E}[|D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}X_j( oldsymbol{z})|^p] igg]. \end{equation} Now we turn back to prove Lemma~ef{lemma:p-norm-h-derivatives-of-XIphi}.  egin{proof}[Proof of Lemma~ef{lemma:p-norm-h-derivatives-of-XIphi}] Since $\partial_\ell$ commutes with translation, we know that \[ (\partial^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\cdot+ oldsymbol{c_I})))( oldsymbol{t})=(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})). \] The same formula holds for $\mathring{X}_k$. Therefore, for a multi-index $ oldsymbol{\alpha}$ with $| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=R$, by Leibniz rule, we have \[ \partial^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{t})=\sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{\alpha}}  rac{ oldsymbol{\alpha}!}{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0! oldsymbol{\alpha}_1!\cdots  oldsymbol{\alpha}_k!}(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0} \varphi_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}))\cdot  igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg]\cdot (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})), \] where we write $ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j=(\alpha_{j,1},\alpha_{j,2},\ldots,\alpha_{j,d})$ and $ oldsymbol{\alpha}=(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\ldots,\alpha_d)$. For clarity, we emphasize that bold symbols such as $ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j$ denote multi-indices, while non-bold symbols like $\alpha_j$ represent scalar components. To bound this sum, our strategy is to estimate each term by applying independence to separate the products, bounding the moments of each derivative factor using Lemma~ef{lemma:p-moment-higher-derivatives-Xj} and Lemma~ef{lemma:pou-scaling-Td}, and finally resumming the bounds via the multinomial theorem. Let $\sum_{j=0}^k  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{\alpha}$ be a fixed partition. By Lemma~ef{lemma:substitue-Xk-ring} and independence of $X_j$'s, we have  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E} igg[ igg|  igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg]\cdot (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg|^p igg]\ &= igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}\mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\cdot \mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] \ & \lesssim \prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]. \end{align*} Since $\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\ge 1$, we can insert at most $R$ terms $X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))$ with $ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{0}$, which gives  egin{align*} \prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]&= igg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j
e  oldsymbol{0}}}\mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\cdot  igg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{0}}}\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\ &\le  igg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j
e 0}} \mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\cdot igg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]. \end{align*} By Lemma~ef{lemma:p-moment-higher-derivatives-Xj}, for each $1\le j\le k$, there exists a constant $M(p, oldsymbol{\alpha}_j)>0$ such that \[ \mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\le M(p, oldsymbol{\alpha}_j) j^{2| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}. \] By Lemma~ef{lemma:pou-scaling-Td}, we have \[ \|D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0}\varphi_k\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^d)}\lesssim 2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|}. \] Thereofre,  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E} igg[ igg|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0} \varphi_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}))\cdot  igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg]\cdot (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg|^p igg]\ &\lesssim 2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|p} igg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\cdot igg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j
e 0}}(M(p, oldsymbol{\alpha}_j)j^{2| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}) igg]. \end{align*} Since the number of non-zero $\alpha_j$ in $\sum_j  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{\alpha}$ is not larger than $A$, we have  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E} igg[ igg|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0} \varphi_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}))\cdot  igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg]\cdot (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg|^p igg]\ &\lesssim 2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|p} igg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\cdot igg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j
e 0}}(M(p, oldsymbol{\alpha}_j)j^{2| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}) igg]. \end{align*} Since the number of non-zero $\alpha_j$ in $\sum_j  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{\alpha}$ is not larger than $A$, we have  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E} igg[ igg|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0} \varphi_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}))\cdot  igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg]\cdot (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg|^p igg]\ &\lesssim \max\Big\{\sup_{| oldsymbol{ eta}|\le A}M(p, oldsymbol{ eta})^A,1\Big\} \cdot  igg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\cdot 2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|p} igg[ \prod_{1\le j\le k} j^{2| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p} igg]\ &\lesssim \sup_{ oldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d} igg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j( oldsymbol{z})|^p] igg]\cdot 2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|p} igg[\prod_{1\le j\le k} j^{2| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p} igg]. \end{align*} By Minkowski inequality, we have  egin{align*} &\quad \, ig(\mathbb{E}[|\partial^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{t})|^p] ig)^{1/p}\ &\lesssim \sup_{ oldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d} igg[\prod_{j=1}^k (\mathbb{E}[|X_j( oldsymbol{z})|^p])^{1/p} igg]\cdot  igg\{\sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{\alpha}} rac{ oldsymbol{\alpha}!}{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0! oldsymbol{\alpha}_1!\cdots  oldsymbol{\alpha}_k!}  igg(2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|}\prod_{1\le j\le k} (j^2 2^j)^{| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|} igg) igg\}. \end{align*} Note that by the definition of the factorial of a multi-index and the separability of the products, the sum can be decomposed over each dimension $\ell=1,\ldots,d$:  egin{align*} \sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{\alpha}} rac{ oldsymbol{\alpha}!}{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0!\cdots  oldsymbol{\alpha}_k!} igg(2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|}\prod_{1\le j\le k} (j^2 2^j)^{| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|} igg)=\prod_{\ell=1}^d \Bigg\{ \sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k \alpha_{j,\ell}=\alpha_\ell} rac{\alpha_\ell!}{\alpha_{0,\ell}!\cdots \alpha_{k,\ell}!} 2^{k\alpha_{0,\ell}} \prod_{1\le j\le k} (j^2 2^j)^{\alpha_{j,\ell}} \Bigg\}. \end{align*} The inner sum for each $\ell$ is now a direct application of the multinomial theorem:  egin{align*} \sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k \alpha_{j,\ell}=\alpha_\ell} rac{\alpha_\ell!}{\alpha_{0,\ell}!\cdots \alpha_{k,\ell}!} 2^{k\alpha_{0,\ell}} \prod_{1\le j\le k} (j^2 2^j)^{\alpha_{j,\ell}} = \left(2^k+\sum_{j=1}^k j^2 2^jight)^{\alpha_\ell}. \end{align*} Substituting this back and combining the exponents, we conclude that  egin{equation*} \left(2^k+\sum_{j=1}^k j^2 2^jight)^{\sum_{\ell=1}^d \alpha_\ell} = \left(2^k+\sum_{j=1}^k j^2 2^jight)^{A}. \end{equation*} Since \[ 2^k+\sum_{j=1}^k j^2 2^j\le 2^k+k^2\sum_{j=0}^k 2^j=2^k+k^2(2^{k+1}-1)\le 3k^2 2^k, \] we conclude that \[  ig(\mathbb{E}[|\partial^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{t})|^p] ig)^{1/p}\lesssim \sup_{ oldsymbol{z}\in T^d} igg[\prod_{j=1}^k (\mathbb{E}[|X_j( oldsymbol{z})|^p])^{1/p} igg]\cdot (k^22^k)^A. \] Taking supremum over $ oldsymbol{t}\in 2^{-k}[-1,1)^d$, we finish the proof. \end{proof}

nodes.name: Replacing centered X_k by X_k in moment bounds
nodes.statement: Let $k\ge 1$ be integer. For any $1\le p<\infty$, there exists a constant $C(p)>0$ depending only on $p$, such that \[ \mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\le C(p)\mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}X_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]. \]
nodes.label: lemma:substitue-Xk-ring

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.8
nodes.statement: Let $\boldsymbol{\alpha}\in \mathbb{N}^d$ be a multi-index. \begin{itemize} \item If $\boldsymbol{\alpha}\ne \boldsymbol{0}$, then \[ (D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))=(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}X_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I})). \] In this case, the equality \[ \mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]=\mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}X_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] \] holds. \item If $\boldsymbol{\alpha}=\boldsymbol{0}$, then \[ \mathbb{E}[|\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]=\mathbb{E}[|X_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))-1|^p]\le 2^{p-1}\big(\mathbb{E}[|X_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]+1\big). \] For $1\le p<\infty$, we have \[ \mathbb{E}[|X_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]=\exp\big(\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}K_k(\boldsymbol{1})\big)\ge 1. \] Thus \[ \mathbb{E}[|\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\le 2^{p-1}\cdot 2\mathbb{E}[|X_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]=2^p\mathbb{E}[|X_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]. \] \end{itemize} If we define $C(p)=2^{p},\forall p\ge 1$, then for any $1\le p<\infty$, \[ \mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\le C(p)\mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}X_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p], \] which proves this lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on alpha: equal derivatives for alpha != 0, and the elementary bound |x-1|^p <= 2^{p-1}(|x|^p+1) with E|X_k|^p >= 1 for alpha = 0.

nodes.name: Fix the multi-index
nodes.statement: Let $\boldsymbol{\alpha}\in \mathbb{N}^d$ be a multi-index.

nodes.name: Case alpha nonzero
nodes.statement: If $\boldsymbol{\alpha}\ne \boldsymbol{0}$, then \[ (D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))=(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}X_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I})). \] In this case, the equality \[ \mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]=\mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}X_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] \] holds.

nodes.name: Case alpha zero
nodes.statement: If $\boldsymbol{\alpha}=\boldsymbol{0}$, then \[ \mathbb{E}[|\mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]=\mathbb{E}[|X_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))-1|^p]\le 2^{p-1}\big(\mathbb{E}[|X_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]+1\big). \]

nodes.name: Take C(p)=2^p
nodes.statement: If we define $C(p)=2^{p},\forall p\ge 1$, then for any $1\le p<\infty$, \[ \mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\le C(p)\mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}X_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p], \] which proves this lemma.

nodes.name: Bound on I_low
nodes.statement: I_{\textnormal{low}}\lesssim 2^{k(-dp+\tau p/2+dp/q)}\cdot \sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k}\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]\bigg].
nodes.label: eq:bound-I-low

nodes.name: Green's second identity
nodes.statement: Let $\Omega$ be a region in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and let $f,g\in C^\infty(\Omega)$. We have \begin{equation} \int_{\Omega}(\Delta f)\cdot g\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}=\int_{\Omega} f\cdot (\Delta g)\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}+\int_{\partial \Omega} \bigg(\frac{\partial f}{\partial \boldsymbol{n}}\cdot g-f\cdot \frac{\partial g}{\partial \boldsymbol{n}}\bigg)\,\mathrm{d}\sigma, \end{equation} where $\frac{\partial f}{\partial \boldsymbol{n}}$ is the normal derivative of $f$ on the boundary $\partial \Omega$ and $\mathrm{d}\sigma$ is the surface measure on $\partial \Omega$.
nodes.label: lemma:Green's-second-id

nodes.name: Green's second identity
nodes.statement: \int_{\Omega}(\Delta f)\cdot g\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}=\int_{\Omega} f\cdot (\Delta g)\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}+\int_{\partial \Omega} \bigg(\frac{\partial f}{\partial \boldsymbol{n}}\cdot g-f\cdot \frac{\partial g}{\partial \boldsymbol{n}}\bigg)\,\mathrm{d}\sigma,
nodes.label: eq:Green's-second-id

nodes.name: Integration by parts against e_n
nodes.statement: \int_{\Omega}(\Delta f)(\boldsymbol{t})\cdot e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}=\int_\Omega f(\boldsymbol{t})\Delta e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}=-4\pi^2|\boldsymbol{n}|^2\int_{\Omega} f(\boldsymbol{t})e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}.
nodes.label: eq:Green's-second-id-2

nodes.name: Integration by parts formula for D_I^phi
nodes.statement: Let $\tau>0$. For each $k\ge 1$, $\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k$ and $\boldsymbol{n}\in \mathbb{Z}^d\setminus\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$, we have \[ \mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n})=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}})(-4\pi^2|\boldsymbol{n}|^2)^{-d}\sum_{|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|=d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}(\partial^{2\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)(\boldsymbol{t})e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}. \]
nodes.label: lemma:integration-by-parts

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.10
nodes.statement: Note that \begin{align*} \mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n})&=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}(\boldsymbol{z}) \bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\boldsymbol{z})\cdot \boldsymbol{z}^{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z})\\ &=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d}\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg] \mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\cdot e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\\ &=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d+\boldsymbol{c_I}}\varphi_{k}(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}-\boldsymbol{c_I}))\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg] \mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\cdot e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}. \end{align*} By changing of variables, we have \begin{align*} \mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n})&=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}})\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d}\varphi_{k}(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t})) \bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))\bigg] \mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))\cdot e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\\ &=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}})\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{t})e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}. \end{align*} Applying \eqref{eq:Green's-second-id-2}, one can obtain \[ \int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{t})e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}=(-4\pi^2 |\boldsymbol{n}|^2)^{-d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}(\Delta^d\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)(\boldsymbol{t}) e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}. \] Therefore \begin{align*} \mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n})&=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}})(-4\pi^2|\boldsymbol{n}|^2)^{-d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}(\Delta^d\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)(\boldsymbol{t})e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\\ &=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}})(-4\pi^2|\boldsymbol{n}|^2)^{-d}\sum_{|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|=d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}(\partial^{2\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)(\boldsymbol{t})e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}. \end{align*} This completes the proof of this lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Change variables to center the cube, then apply Green's identity d times to the compactly supported smooth function X_I^phi.

nodes.name: Rewrite in Euclidean coordinates
nodes.statement: Note that \begin{align*} \mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n})&=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}(\boldsymbol{z}) \bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})\bigg]\mathring{X}_k(\boldsymbol{z})\cdot \boldsymbol{z}^{\boldsymbol{n}}\,\boldsymbol{m}(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{z})\\ &=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d}\varphi_{\boldsymbol{I}}(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg] \mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\cdot e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\\ &=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d+\boldsymbol{c_I}}\varphi_{k}(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}-\boldsymbol{c_I}))\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\bigg] \mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\cdot e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Translate by c_I
nodes.statement: By changing of variables, we have \begin{align*} \mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n})&=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}})\int_{[-1/2,1/2)^d}\varphi_{k}(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t})) \bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))\bigg] \mathring{X}_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))\cdot e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\\ &=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}})\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{t})e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Apply Green's identity d times
nodes.statement: Applying \eqref{eq:Green's-second-id-2}, one can obtain \[ \int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{t})e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}=(-4\pi^2 |\boldsymbol{n}|^2)^{-d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}(\Delta^d\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)(\boldsymbol{t}) e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}. \]

nodes.name: Expand Delta^d into partial derivatives
nodes.statement: Therefore \begin{align*} \mathfrak{D}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{n})&=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}})(-4\pi^2|\boldsymbol{n}|^2)^{-d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}(\Delta^d\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)(\boldsymbol{t})e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\\ &=\langle \boldsymbol{n}\rangle^{\tau/2}e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}})(-4\pi^2|\boldsymbol{n}|^2)^{-d}\sum_{|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|=d}\int_{2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}(\partial^{2\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi)(\boldsymbol{t})e_{\boldsymbol{n}}(\boldsymbol{t})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}. \end{align*} This completes the proof of this lemma.

nodes.name: Moments of higher derivatives of X_I^phi
nodes.statement: For any $1\le p<\infty$, and any integer $A\ge 0$, we have \[ \sup_{|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|=A}\sup_{\boldsymbol{t}\in 2^{-k}[-1,1)^d}\big(\mathbb{E}[|\partial^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{t})|^p]\big)^{1/p}\lesssim \sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{1\le j\le k}\big(\mathbb{E}[|D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]\big)^{1/p}\bigg]\cdot (k^2 2^k)^{A}, \] where the implicit constant is independent of $k$ and $\boldsymbol{I}$.
nodes.label: lemma:p-norm-h-derivatives-of-XIphi

nodes.name: Bound on I_high
nodes.statement: I_{\textnormal{high}}\lesssim k^{4dp}\cdot 2^{k(-dp+\tau p/2+dp/q)}\cdot \sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{1\le j\le k}\mathbb{E}[|D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]\bigg].
nodes.label: eq:bound-I-high

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.11
nodes.statement:
Since $\partial_\ell$ commutes with translation, we know that \[ (\partial^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\cdot+ oldsymbol{c_I})))( oldsymbol{t})=(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})). \] The same formula holds for $\mathring{X}_k$. Therefore, for a multi-index $ oldsymbol{\alpha}$ with $| oldsymbol{\alpha}|=R$, by Leibniz rule, we have \[ \partial^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{t})=\sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{\alpha}}  rac{ oldsymbol{\alpha}!}{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0! oldsymbol{\alpha}_1!\cdots  oldsymbol{\alpha}_k!}(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0} \varphi_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}))\cdot  igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg]\cdot (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})), \] where we write $ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j=(\alpha_{j,1},\alpha_{j,2},\ldots,\alpha_{j,d})$ and $ oldsymbol{\alpha}=(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\ldots,\alpha_d)$. For clarity, we emphasize that bold symbols such as $ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j$ denote multi-indices, while non-bold symbols like $\alpha_j$ represent scalar components. To bound this sum, our strategy is to estimate each term by applying independence to separate the products, bounding the moments of each derivative factor using Lemma~ef{lemma:p-moment-higher-derivatives-Xj} and Lemma~ef{lemma:pou-scaling-Td}, and finally resumming the bounds via the multinomial theorem. Let $\sum_{j=0}^k  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{\alpha}$ be a fixed partition. By Lemma~ef{lemma:substitue-Xk-ring} and independence of $X_j$'s, we have  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E} igg[ igg|  igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg]\cdot (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg|^p igg]\ &= igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}\mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\cdot \mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] \ & \lesssim \prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]. \end{align*} Since $\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\ge 1$, we can insert at most $R$ terms $X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))$ with $ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{0}$, which gives  egin{align*} \prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]&= igg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j
e  oldsymbol{0}}}\mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\cdot  igg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{0}}}\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\ &\le  igg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j
e 0}} \mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\cdot igg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]. \end{align*} By Lemma~ef{lemma:p-moment-higher-derivatives-Xj}, for each $1\le j\le k$, there exists a constant $M(p, oldsymbol{\alpha}_j)>0$ such that \[ \mathbb{E}[|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\le M(p, oldsymbol{\alpha}_j) j^{2| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}. \] By Lemma~ef{lemma:pou-scaling-Td}, we have \[ \|D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0}\varphi_k\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^d)}\lesssim 2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|}. \] Thereofre,  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E} igg[ igg|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0} \varphi_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}))\cdot  igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg]\cdot (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg|^p igg]\ &\lesssim 2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|p} igg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\cdot igg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j
e 0}}(M(p, oldsymbol{\alpha}_j)j^{2| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}) igg]. \end{align*} Since the number of non-zero $\alpha_j$ in $\sum_j  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{\alpha}$ is not larger than $A$, we have  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E} igg[ igg|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0} \varphi_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}))\cdot  igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg]\cdot (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg|^p igg]\ &\lesssim 2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|p} igg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\cdot igg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j
e 0}}(M(p, oldsymbol{\alpha}_j)j^{2| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}) igg]. \end{align*} Since the number of non-zero $\alpha_j$ in $\sum_j  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{\alpha}$ is not larger than $A$, we have  egin{align*} &\mathbb{E} igg[ igg|(D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0} \varphi_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}))\cdot  igg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg]\cdot (D^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I})) igg|^p igg]\ &\lesssim \max\Big\{\sup_{| oldsymbol{ eta}|\le A}M(p, oldsymbol{ eta})^A,1\Big\} \cdot  igg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}( oldsymbol{t}+ oldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] igg]\cdot 2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|p} igg[ \prod_{1\le j\le k} j^{2| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p} igg]\ &\lesssim \sup_{ oldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d} igg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j( oldsymbol{z})|^p] igg]\cdot 2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|p} igg[\prod_{1\le j\le k} j^{2| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p} igg]. \end{align*} By Minkowski inequality, we have  egin{align*} &\quad \, ig(\mathbb{E}[|\partial^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{t})|^p] ig)^{1/p}\ &\lesssim \sup_{ oldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d} igg[\prod_{j=1}^k (\mathbb{E}[|X_j( oldsymbol{z})|^p])^{1/p} igg]\cdot  igg\{\sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{\alpha}} rac{ oldsymbol{\alpha}!}{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0! oldsymbol{\alpha}_1!\cdots  oldsymbol{\alpha}_k!}  igg(2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|}\prod_{1\le j\le k} (j^2 2^j)^{| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|} igg) igg\}. \end{align*} Note that by the definition of the factorial of a multi-index and the separability of the products, the sum can be decomposed over each dimension $\ell=1,\ldots,d$:  egin{align*} \sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k  oldsymbol{\alpha}_j= oldsymbol{\alpha}} rac{ oldsymbol{\alpha}!}{ oldsymbol{\alpha}_0!\cdots  oldsymbol{\alpha}_k!} igg(2^{k| oldsymbol{\alpha}_0|}\prod_{1\le j\le k} (j^2 2^j)^{| oldsymbol{\alpha}_j|} igg)=\prod_{\ell=1}^d \Bigg\{ \sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k \alpha_{j,\ell}=\alpha_\ell} rac{\alpha_\ell!}{\alpha_{0,\ell}!\cdots \alpha_{k,\ell}!} 2^{k\alpha_{0,\ell}} \prod_{1\le j\le k} (j^2 2^j)^{\alpha_{j,\ell}} \Bigg\}. \end{align*} The inner sum for each $\ell$ is now a direct application of the multinomial theorem:  egin{align*} \sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k \alpha_{j,\ell}=\alpha_\ell} rac{\alpha_\ell!}{\alpha_{0,\ell}!\cdots \alpha_{k,\ell}!} 2^{k\alpha_{0,\ell}} \prod_{1\le j\le k} (j^2 2^j)^{\alpha_{j,\ell}} = \left(2^k+\sum_{j=1}^k j^2 2^jight)^{\alpha_\ell}. \end{align*} Substituting this back and combining the exponents, we conclude that  egin{equation*} \left(2^k+\sum_{j=1}^k j^2 2^jight)^{\sum_{\ell=1}^d \alpha_\ell} = \left(2^k+\sum_{j=1}^k j^2 2^jight)^{A}. \end{equation*} Since \[ 2^k+\sum_{j=1}^k j^2 2^j\le 2^k+k^2\sum_{j=0}^k 2^j=2^k+k^2(2^{k+1}-1)\le 3k^2 2^k, \] we conclude that \[  ig(\mathbb{E}[|\partial^{ oldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{ oldsymbol{I}}^\varphi( oldsymbol{t})|^p] ig)^{1/p}\lesssim \sup_{ oldsymbol{z}\in T^d} igg[\prod_{j=1}^k (\mathbb{E}[|X_j( oldsymbol{z})|^p])^{1/p} igg]\cdot (k^22^k)^A. \] Taking supremum over $ oldsymbol{t}\in 2^{-k}[-1,1)^d$, we finish the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Leibniz rule, independence, the derivative bounds of Lemmas 4.6 and 2.3, and resummation by the multinomial theorem. Key step: the multinomial sum equals (2^k+sum j^2 2^j)^A <= (3k^2 2^k)^A.

nodes.name: Derivatives commute with translation
nodes.statement: Since $\partial_\ell$ commutes with translation, we know that \[ (\partial^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}X_j(\mathcal{E}(\cdot+\boldsymbol{c_I})))(\boldsymbol{t})=(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}X_j)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I})). \] The same formula holds for $\mathring{X}_k$.

nodes.name: Leibniz rule expansion
nodes.statement: Therefore, for a multi-index $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$ with $|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|=R$, by Leibniz rule, we have \[ \partial^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{t})=\sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k \boldsymbol{\alpha}_j=\boldsymbol{\alpha}} \frac{\boldsymbol{\alpha}!}{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_0!\boldsymbol{\alpha}_1!\cdots \boldsymbol{\alpha}_k!}(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_0} \varphi_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\cdot \bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))\bigg]\cdot (D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I})), \] where we write $\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j=(\alpha_{j,1},\alpha_{j,2},\ldots,\alpha_{j,d})$ and $\boldsymbol{\alpha}=(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\ldots,\alpha_d)$. For clarity, we emphasize that bold symbols such as $\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j$ denote multi-indices, while non-bold symbols like $\alpha_j$ represent scalar components.

nodes.name: Outline: independence
nodes.statement: To bound this sum, our strategy is to estimate each term by applying independence to separate the products, bounding the moments of each derivative factor using Lemma~\ref{lemma:p-moment-higher-derivatives-Xj} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:pou-scaling-Td}, and finally resumming the bounds via the multinomial theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Outline: independence, moment bounds, multinomial resummation

nodes.name: Factor moments by independence and Lemma 4.8
nodes.statement: Let $\sum_{j=0}^k \boldsymbol{\alpha}_j=\boldsymbol{\alpha}$ be a fixed partition. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:substitue-Xk-ring} and independence of $X_j$'s, we have \begin{align*} &\mathbb{E}\bigg[\bigg| \bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))\bigg]\cdot (D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))\bigg|^p\bigg]\\ &=\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}\mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\bigg]\cdot \mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p] \\ & \lesssim \prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Factor moments by independence and Lemma 4.8

nodes.name: Insert undifferentiated factors
nodes.statement: Since $\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\ge 1$, we can insert at most $R$ terms $X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))$ with $\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j=\boldsymbol{0}$, which gives \begin{align*} \prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]&=\bigg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\\ \boldsymbol{\alpha}_j\ne \boldsymbol{0}}}\mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\bigg]\cdot \bigg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\\ \boldsymbol{\alpha}_j=\boldsymbol{0}}}\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\bigg]\\ &\le \bigg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\\ \boldsymbol{\alpha}_j\ne 0}} \mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\bigg]\cdot\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\bigg]. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Derivative moments by Lemma 4.6
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lemma:p-moment-higher-derivatives-Xj}, for each $1\le j\le k$, there exists a constant $M(p,\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j)>0$ such that \[ \mathbb{E}[|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\le M(p,\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j) j^{2|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}. \]

nodes.name: Window derivative bounds by Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lemma:pou-scaling-Td}, we have \[ \|D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_0}\varphi_k\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^d)}\lesssim 2^{k|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_0|}. \]

nodes.name: Combine the factor bounds
nodes.statement: Thereofre, \begin{align*} &\mathbb{E}\bigg[\bigg|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_0} \varphi_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\cdot \bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))\bigg]\cdot (D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))\bigg|^p\bigg]\\ &\lesssim 2^{k|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_0|p}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\bigg]\cdot\bigg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\\\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j\ne 0}}(M(p,\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j)j^{2|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p})\bigg]. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Bound constants uniformly
nodes.statement: Since the number of non-zero $\alpha_j$ in $\sum_j \boldsymbol{\alpha}_j=\boldsymbol{\alpha}$ is not larger than $A$, we have \begin{align*} &\mathbb{E}\bigg[\bigg|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_0} \varphi_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\cdot \bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))\bigg]\cdot (D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))\bigg|^p\bigg]\\ &\lesssim 2^{k|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_0|p}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\bigg]\cdot\bigg[\prod_{\substack{1\le j\le k,\\\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j\ne 0}}(M(p,\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j)j^{2|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p})\bigg]. \end{align*} Since the number of non-zero $\alpha_j$ in $\sum_j \boldsymbol{\alpha}_j=\boldsymbol{\alpha}$ is not larger than $A$, we have \begin{align*} &\mathbb{E}\bigg[\bigg|(D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_0} \varphi_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))\cdot \bigg[\prod_{j=1}^{k-1} (D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j}X_j)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))\bigg]\cdot (D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_k}\mathring{X}_k)(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))\bigg|^p\bigg]\\ &\lesssim \max\Big\{\sup_{|\boldsymbol{\beta}|\le A}M(p,\boldsymbol{\beta})^A,1\Big\} \cdot \bigg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}+\boldsymbol{c_I}))|^p]\bigg]\cdot 2^{k|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_0|p}\bigg[ \prod_{1\le j\le k} j^{2|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}\bigg]\\ &\lesssim \sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^k \mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p]\bigg]\cdot 2^{k|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_0|p}\bigg[\prod_{1\le j\le k} j^{2|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}2^{j|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j|p}\bigg]. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Minkowski over the Leibniz sum
nodes.statement: By Minkowski inequality, we have \begin{align*} &\quad \,\big(\mathbb{E}[|\partial^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{t})|^p]\big)^{1/p}\\ &\lesssim \sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in \mathbb{T}^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^k (\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p])^{1/p}\bigg]\cdot \bigg\{\sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k \boldsymbol{\alpha}_j=\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\frac{\boldsymbol{\alpha}!}{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_0!\boldsymbol{\alpha}_1!\cdots \boldsymbol{\alpha}_k!} \bigg(2^{k|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_0|}\prod_{1\le j\le k} (j^2 2^j)^{|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j|}\bigg)\bigg\}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Resum by the multinomial theorem
nodes.statement: Note that by the definition of the factorial of a multi-index and the separability of the products, the sum can be decomposed over each dimension $\ell=1,\ldots,d$: \begin{align*} \sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k \boldsymbol{\alpha}_j=\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\frac{\boldsymbol{\alpha}!}{\boldsymbol{\alpha}_0!\cdots \boldsymbol{\alpha}_k!}\bigg(2^{k|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_0|}\prod_{1\le j\le k} (j^2 2^j)^{|\boldsymbol{\alpha}_j|}\bigg)=\prod_{\ell=1}^d \Bigg\{ \sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k \alpha_{j,\ell}=\alpha_\ell}\frac{\alpha_\ell!}{\alpha_{0,\ell}!\cdots \alpha_{k,\ell}!} 2^{k\alpha_{0,\ell}} \prod_{1\le j\le k} (j^2 2^j)^{\alpha_{j,\ell}} \Bigg\}. \end{align*} The inner sum for each $\ell$ is now a direct application of the multinomial theorem: \begin{align*} \sum_{\sum_{j=0}^k \alpha_{j,\ell}=\alpha_\ell}\frac{\alpha_\ell!}{\alpha_{0,\ell}!\cdots \alpha_{k,\ell}!} 2^{k\alpha_{0,\ell}} \prod_{1\le j\le k} (j^2 2^j)^{\alpha_{j,\ell}} = \left(2^k+\sum_{j=1}^k j^2 2^j\right)^{\alpha_\ell}. \end{align*} Substituting this back and combining the exponents, we conclude that \begin{equation*} \left(2^k+\sum_{j=1}^k j^2 2^j\right)^{\sum_{\ell=1}^d \alpha_\ell} = \left(2^k+\sum_{j=1}^k j^2 2^j\right)^{A}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Bound 2^k+sum j^2 2^j by 3k^2 2^k
nodes.statement: Since \[ 2^k+\sum_{j=1}^k j^2 2^j\le 2^k+k^2\sum_{j=0}^k 2^j=2^k+k^2(2^{k+1}-1)\le 3k^2 2^k, \] we conclude that \[ \big(\mathbb{E}[|\partial^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\mathcal{X}_{\boldsymbol{I}}^\varphi(\boldsymbol{t})|^p]\big)^{1/p}\lesssim \sup_{\boldsymbol{z}\in T^d}\bigg[\prod_{j=1}^k (\mathbb{E}[|X_j(\boldsymbol{z})|^p])^{1/p}\bigg]\cdot (k^22^k)^A. \]

nodes.name: Take supremum over t
nodes.statement: Taking supremum over $\boldsymbol{t}\in 2^{-k}[-1,1)^d$, we finish the proof.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.3 (construction of the partition of unity)
nodes.statement: In this appendix, we aim to prove Lemma~\ref{lemma:pou-scaling-Td}. The construction of partition of unity with scaling property on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\mathbb{T}^d$ is well-known in harmonic analysis, especially in the context of wave packet analysis and time-frequency analysis (e.g.,~\cite[Chapter~2]{Dem20}). For convenience, we shall exhibit the construction here. Although a partition of unity on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\mathbb{T}^d$ could be constructed directly, we opt for a more intuitive approach by first building a one-dimensional partition of unity on $\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{T}$ and then extending it to higher dimensions via a tensor product. \medskip {\flushleft \bf Step 1. Construction of partition of unity on $\mathbb{R}$.} \medskip A standard choice of bump function $\vartheta\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R})$ with $\operatorname{supp} \vartheta \subset [-1,1]$ is given by \[ \vartheta(t)=\begin{cases} e^{-1/(1-t^2)},& |t|\le 1,\\ 0,& |t|> 1. \end{cases} \] Then $W(t)\coloneq \sum_{h\in \mathbb{Z}}\vartheta(t-h)$ is a periodic function with $W(t+1)=W(t)$. Note that the summation in the definition of $W$ is locally finite, and the sum is strictly positive for $t\in \mathbb{R}$. We can define \[ \theta(t)\coloneq \frac{\vartheta(t)}{W(t)},\quad \forall t\in \mathbb{R}. \] Then $\theta\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R})$, $\operatorname{supp} \theta\subset [-1,1]$, and \[ \sum_{h\in \mathbb{Z}}\theta(t-h)=\sum_{h\in \mathbb{Z}}\frac{\vartheta(t-h)}{W(t-h)}=\frac{1}{W(t)}\sum_{h\in \mathbb{Z}}\vartheta(t-h)=1,\quad \forall t\in \mathbb{R}. \] Therefore, $\{\theta(\cdot-h)\}_{h\in \mathbb{Z}}$ forms a partition of unity on $\mathbb{R}$ and the support of each $\theta(\cdot-h)$ is contained in $[-1,1]+h$. We can now introduce the scaling of $\theta$. Let $k \ge 1$. For each $I\in \widetilde{\mathscr{D}}_k^1$, we define \[ \theta_{I}(t)\coloneq \theta(2^k(t-c_{I})),\quad \forall t\in \mathbb{R}. \] Here, $c_{I}$ is the center of the cube $I=[0,2^{-k})+2^{-k}h$, that is, $c_{I}=2^{-k}(2^{-1}+h)$. We claim that \begin{equation} \sum_{I\in \widetilde{\mathscr{D}}_k^1} \theta_{I}(t)=1,\quad \forall t\in \mathbb{R}. \end{equation} Moreover, the support of $\theta_{I}$ is contained in $2I$. In fact, for any $t\in \mathbb{R}$, we have \begin{align*} \sum_{I\in \widetilde{\mathscr{D}}_k^1} \theta_{I}(t)&=\sum_{I\in \widetilde{\mathscr{D}}_k^1} \theta(2^k(t-c_{I}))=\sum_{h\in \mathbb{Z}}\theta(2^k(t-2^{-k}(2^{-1}+h)))=\sum_{h\in \mathbb{Z}}\theta((2^k t-2^{-1})-h)=1. \end{align*} This proves \eqref{eq:pou-R-scaling-1D}. \medskip {\flushleft \bf Step 2. Construction of partition of unity on $\mathbb{T}$.} \medskip The second step is to transplant the partition of unity on $\mathbb{R}$ to $\mathbb{T}$. Define \[ \rho(e(t))\coloneq \theta(t),\quad \forall t\in [-1/2,1/2), \] and \[ \rho_k(e(t))\coloneq \theta(2^k t),\quad \forall t\in [-1/2,1/2). \] From the definition, we easily see that $\rho_k\in C^\infty(\mathbb{T})$ and \[ \operatorname{supp} \rho_k\subset \overline{B}(1,2^{-k})=e([-2^{-k},2^{-k}]). \] The partition of unity on $\mathbb{T}$ at scale $2^{-k}$ is again generated by the translation of $\rho_k$, that is, \[ \sum_{I\in \mathscr{D}_k^1} \rho_k(e(t-c_I))=\sum_{I\in \mathscr{D}_k^1} \theta_{I}(t)=1,\quad \forall t\in [-1/2,1/2). \] Define $\rho_{I}(e(t))\coloneq \rho_k(e(t-c_{I}))$ for each $I\in \mathscr{D}_k^1$ and $t\in [-1/2,1/2)$. Then the equation above can be rewritten as \[ \sum_{I\in \mathscr{D}_k^1} \rho_{I}(z)=1,\quad \forall z\in \mathbb{T}. \] Note that $\rho_k(e(\cdot-c_I))$ is nothing but the periodization of $\theta(2^k(\cdot -c_I))$, which means \[ \rho_k(e(t-c_I))=\sum_{h\in \mathbb{Z}} \theta(2^k(t-c_I-h)). \] Taking sum over all $I\in \mathscr{D}_k^1$, we have \[ \sum_{I\in \mathscr{D}_k^1} \rho_k(e(t-c_I))=\sum_{I\in \mathscr{D}_k^1}\sum_{h\in \mathbb{Z}} \theta(2^k(t-c_I-h))=\sum_{I\in \widetilde{\mathscr{D}}_k^1} \theta_I(t)=1,\quad \forall t\in \mathbb{R}. \] \medskip {\flushleft \bf Step 3. Construct partition of unity on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:pou-scaling-Td}.} \medskip Now we can naturally define partition of unity on $\mathbb{T}^d$ by tensor product. Define \[ \varphi_k(\boldsymbol{z})=\varphi(z_1,z_2,\ldots,z_d)\coloneq \prod_{\ell=1}^d\rho_k(z_\ell),\quad \forall \boldsymbol{z}=(z_1,z_2,\ldots,z_d)\in \mathbb{T}^d. \] We claim that $\varphi_k$ is the desired function in Lemma~\ref{lemma:pou-scaling-Td}. By definition, for any $\boldsymbol{t}\in \mathbb{R}^d$, we have \[ \sum_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k^d} \varphi_{k}(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}-\boldsymbol{c}_{\boldsymbol{I}}))=\sum_{\boldsymbol{I}\in \mathscr{D}_k^d} \prod_{\ell=1}^d \rho_{I_\ell}(e(t_\ell-c_{I_\ell})), \] where $\boldsymbol{I}=I_1\times I_2\times\cdots \times I_d$ and $I_\ell\in \mathscr{D}_k^1$ for each $\ell=1,2,\ldots,d$. Then \[ \sum_{\boldsymbol{I} \in \mathscr{D}_k^d} \prod_{\ell=1}^d \rho_{I_\ell}(e(t_\ell-c_{I_\ell}))=\prod_{\ell=1}^d \bigg[\sum_{I_\ell \in \mathscr{D}_k^1} \rho_{k}(e(t_\ell-c_\ell))\bigg]=1. \] This proves \eqref{eq:pou-Td-euclidean-coordinate} in Lemma~\ref{lemma:pou-scaling-Td}. Note that \[ \operatorname{supp} \varphi_k=\prod_{\ell=1}^d \operatorname{supp} \rho_k\subset \prod_{\ell=1}^d e([-2^{-k},2^{-k}])=\mathcal{E}([-2^{-k},2^{-k}]^d), \] which is (2) in Lemma~\ref{lemma:pou-scaling-Td}. Now we prove (3) in Lemma~\ref{lemma:pou-scaling-Td}. By definition, for any multi-index $\boldsymbol{\alpha}=(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\ldots,\alpha_d)\in \mathbb{N}^d$ and $\boldsymbol{t}=(t_1,t_2,\ldots,t_d)\in \mathbb{R}^d$, we have \[ D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\varphi_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))=\prod_{\ell=1}^d \frac{\mathrm{d}^{\alpha_\ell}}{\mathrm{d}t_\ell^{\alpha_\ell}}\rho_k(e(t_\ell-c_{I_\ell})). \] But \begin{align*} \frac{\mathrm{d}^{\alpha_\ell}}{\mathrm{d}t_\ell^{\alpha_\ell}}\rho_k(e(t_\ell-c_{I_\ell}))&=\frac{\mathrm{d}^{\alpha_\ell}}{\mathrm{d}t_\ell^{\alpha_\ell}}\bigg[\sum_{h\in \mathbb{Z}} \theta(2^k(t_\ell-c_{I_\ell}-h))\bigg] \\ &=\sum_{h\in \mathbb{Z}} \frac{\mathrm{d}^{\alpha_\ell}}{\mathrm{d}t_\ell^{\alpha_\ell}}\theta(2^k(t_\ell-c_{I_\ell}-h))\\ &=\sum_{h\in \mathbb{Z}} 2^{k\alpha_\ell}\bigg(\frac{\mathrm{d}^{\alpha_\ell}}{\mathrm{d}t^{\alpha_\ell}}\theta\bigg)(2^k(t_\ell-c_{I_\ell}-h)). \end{align*} Since summands have disjoint supports, we have \[ \bigg\|D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\varphi_k\bigg\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^d)}\le \prod_{\ell=1}^d 2^{k\alpha_\ell}\bigg\|\frac{\mathrm{d}^{\alpha_\ell}}{\mathrm{d}t^{\alpha_\ell}}\theta\bigg\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{R})}\le 2^{k|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|}\|\theta\|_{C^{|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|}(\mathbb{R})}^d, \] which implies (3) in Lemma~\ref{lemma:pou-scaling-Td}.

nodes.name: Derivative scaling (3)
nodes.statement: Now we prove (3) in Lemma~\ref{lemma:pou-scaling-Td}. By definition, for any multi-index $\boldsymbol{\alpha}=(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\ldots,\alpha_d)\in \mathbb{N}^d$ and $\boldsymbol{t}=(t_1,t_2,\ldots,t_d)\in \mathbb{R}^d$, we have \[ D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\varphi_k(\mathcal{E}(\boldsymbol{t}))=\prod_{\ell=1}^d \frac{\mathrm{d}^{\alpha_\ell}}{\mathrm{d}t_\ell^{\alpha_\ell}}\rho_k(e(t_\ell-c_{I_\ell})). \] But \begin{align*} \frac{\mathrm{d}^{\alpha_\ell}}{\mathrm{d}t_\ell^{\alpha_\ell}}\rho_k(e(t_\ell-c_{I_\ell}))&=\frac{\mathrm{d}^{\alpha_\ell}}{\mathrm{d}t_\ell^{\alpha_\ell}}\bigg[\sum_{h\in \mathbb{Z}} \theta(2^k(t_\ell-c_{I_\ell}-h))\bigg] \\ &=\sum_{h\in \mathbb{Z}} \frac{\mathrm{d}^{\alpha_\ell}}{\mathrm{d}t_\ell^{\alpha_\ell}}\theta(2^k(t_\ell-c_{I_\ell}-h))\\ &=\sum_{h\in \mathbb{Z}} 2^{k\alpha_\ell}\bigg(\frac{\mathrm{d}^{\alpha_\ell}}{\mathrm{d}t^{\alpha_\ell}}\theta\bigg)(2^k(t_\ell-c_{I_\ell}-h)). \end{align*} Since summands have disjoint supports, we have \[ \bigg\|D^{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}\varphi_k\bigg\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^d)}\le \prod_{\ell=1}^d 2^{k\alpha_\ell}\bigg\|\frac{\mathrm{d}^{\alpha_\ell}}{\mathrm{d}t^{\alpha_\ell}}\theta\bigg\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{R})}\le 2^{k|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|}\|\theta\|_{C^{|\boldsymbol{\alpha}|}(\mathbb{R})}^d, \] which implies (3) in Lemma~\ref{lemma:pou-scaling-Td}.
